title.en: Volume 291 Biographies 78: Hai Wang, Mang Gu Li, Hang Yilu, Fu Ding, Chen Yi, Liu Shishu, Wang Guodong
title.raw: 卷291 列傳七十八 海望 莽鹄立 杭奕禄 傅鼎 陈仪 刘师恕 王国栋

sentences.zh: 列傳七十八

translations.literal: Biographies 78
translations.idiomatic: Biography 78

sentences.zh: 海望三和莽鵠立杭奕祿傅鼐陳儀劉師恕焦祈年李徽

translations.literal: Hai Wang, San He, Mang Hulu, Hang Yilu, Fu Nai, Chen Yi, Liu Shishu, Jiao Qinian, and Li Hui
translations.idiomatic: Hai Wang, San He, Mang Hulu, Hang Yilu, Fu Nai, Chen Yi, Liu Shishu, Jiao Qinian, and Li Hui

sentences.zh: 王國棟許容蔡仕舢

translations.literal: Wang Guodong, Xu Rong, and Cai Shinan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guodong, Xu Rong, and Cai Shinan

sentences.zh: 海望，烏雅氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Hai Wang, of the Uya clan, was a Bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Hai Wang, of the Uya clan, came from the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 初授護軍校。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed a Guard Lieutenant.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a Guard Lieutenant.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，擢內務府主事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, he was promoted to Director in the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign, he was raised to Director in the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中，充崇文門監督。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Bureau Director and appointed Supervisor of Chongwen Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Bureau Director and served as Supervisor of Chongwen Gate.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢總管內務府大臣，兼管戶部三庫，賜二品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was promoted to Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Department, with concurrent charge of the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue, and was granted the second-rank official hat knob.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, he became Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Department, took concurrent charge of the Ministry of Revenue's three treasuries, and received the second-rank hat knob.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷戶部侍郎，仍兼管內務府，授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, still concurrently managing the Imperial Household Department, and was appointed Grand Minister of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, he was made Vice Minister of Revenue while retaining the Imperial Household Department, and was appointed a Grand Minister of the Interior.

sentences.zh: 十一年，命偕直隸總督李衛勘浙江海塘，與衛議奏在海寧尖、塔兩山間建石壩，使海潮外趨，並在仁和、海寧兩縣境改建大石塘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was ordered together with Li Wei, Governor-General of Zhili, to survey Zhejiang's sea embankments; with Wei he jointly memorialized to build stone dams between Jianshan and Tashan at Haining, diverting the tidal surge outward, and to rebuild major stone embankments in the territories of Renhe and Haining counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, he was sent with Zhili governor-general Li Wei to inspect Zhejiang's sea walls. Together they memorialized for stone dams between Jian and Ta Hills at Haining to drive the tide seaward, and for major stone revetments across Renhe and Haining.

sentences.zh: 上命浙江總督程元章相度遵行。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Cheng Yuanzhang, Governor-General of Zhejiang, to inspect the ground and carry it out accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Zhejiang governor-general Cheng Yuanzhang to survey the works and implement the plan.

sentences.zh: 又奏請設專官總轄，令駐防將軍、副都統協同監修，及議敘在工人員工價以銀米兼發，並從之。

translations.literal: They also memorialized requesting a dedicated official to oversee the whole project, that the garrison general and vice commandant-in-chief assist in supervision and repair, and that rewards for workers be paid in both silver and grain; all was approved.
translations.idiomatic: They further asked for a special overseer, garrison generals and vice commandants to help supervise construction, and worker wages paid in silver and grain alike—all of which was granted.

sentences.zh: 十三年，振武將軍傅爾丹虐兵婪索事發，命海望赴北路軍營逮治。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the case of General Zhenwu Fu Erdan's abuse and extortion of troops came to light; Hai Wang was ordered to proceed to the northern-route army camp to arrest and try him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, after Fu Erdan, the Zhenwu general, was exposed for brutalizing and extorting his troops, Hai Wang was dispatched to the northern army to take him into custody and try him.

sentences.zh: 尋命辦理軍機事務。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was ordered to handle Grand Council affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 世宗疾大漸，召同受顧命。

translations.literal: As Emperor Yongzheng's illness grew critically severe, he was summoned together to receive the imperial testament.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yongzheng's illness turned grave, he was called in as one of the testamentary ministers.

sentences.zh: 是時辦理軍機事務鄂爾泰、張廷玉、訥親、班第、索柱、豐盛額、莽鵠立、納延泰及海望凡九人。

translations.literal: At that time those handling Grand Council affairs were Ortai, Zhang Tingyu, Necin, Bandi, Suozhu, Fengshen'e, Mang Hulu, Nayantai, and Hai Wang—nine in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Council at that time numbered nine: Ortai, Zhang Tingyu, Necin, Bandi, Suozhu, Fengshen'e, Mang Hulu, Nayantai, and Hai Wang.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，命尚書徐本入直。

translations.literal: Upon Emperor Qianlong's accession, he ordered Minister Xu Ben to enter regular attendance.
translations.idiomatic: After Qianlong took the throne, he ordered Minister Xu Ben to join the council in regular attendance.

sentences.zh: 旋設總理事務處，命鄂爾泰、廷玉總理，本、訥親及海望協辦，班第、納延泰、索柱差委辦事。

translations.literal: Soon the Office for General Management of Affairs was established; Ortai and Tingyu were ordered to direct it, with Ben, Necin, and Hai Wang to assist, while Bandi, Nayantai, and Suozhu were assigned to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The General Affairs Office was then set up under Ortai and Zhang Tingyu, with Xu Ben, Necin, and Hai Wang as assistants; Bandi, Nayantai, and Suozhu were detailed to carry out its business.

sentences.zh: 尋命海望署戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Hai Wang was ordered to act as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Hai Wang was soon made acting Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 海望還自軍前，奏言：「鄂爾坤發遣罪人種地無實效，且恐生事，當改發他處。

translations.literal: Hai Wang, returning from the front, memorialized: "Sending exiled criminals to farm at Erkun has yielded no real effect and may breed trouble; they should be reassigned elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from the army, Hai Wang reported that farming by exiles sent to Erkun had proved ineffective, might stir unrest, and ought to be moved elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 」世宗謂：「鄂爾坤方駐兵，當可彈壓，海望奏非是。

translations.literal: " Emperor Yongzheng said: "Troops are now stationed at Erkun and can suppress them; Hai Wang's memorial is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Yongzheng had said: "Erkun is garrisoned and can hold them down—Hai Wang is mistaken."

sentences.zh: 」高宗以海望奏下總理事務處議，議上，上諭曰：「海望奏，前奉皇考申飭。

translations.literal: " Emperor Qianlong referred Hai Wang's memorial to the General Affairs Office for deliberation; when the reply was submitted, the Emperor instructed: "Hai Wang's memorial was once sternly rebuked by my late father.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Qianlong sent the memorial to the General Affairs Office. When their reply came up, he instructed: "Hai Wang's memorial was once sharply rebuked by my late father.

sentences.zh: 朕推皇考之意，蓋以發遣罪人，皆身獲重罪，今令軍前種地，乃所以保全之。

translations.literal: As I infer my late father's intent, it was that the exiled criminals had all incurred grave offenses, and sending them to farm before the army was meant to preserve them.
translations.idiomatic: I read my father's meaning this way: these men had all committed serious crimes, yet service farming with the troops was meant to spare their lives.

sentences.zh: 其中若有冤抑，自應聲明具奏寬釋。

translations.literal: If any among them suffered wrongful oppression, they should of course state it clearly in a memorial and seek release.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone truly wronged should say so plainly in a memorial and ask to be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 如但以不善開墾，遂爾改發內地，此曹既獲重罪，又不肯急公趨事，轉得遂其僥倖之心；

translations.literal: But if they are merely poor at opening land and for that reason are reassigned inland, these fellows, having already incurred grave offenses, yet refuse to serve the public good with urgency, and instead have their hearts of lucky escape fulfilled;
translations.idiomatic: Yet if poor farming alone becomes grounds to send them back inland, men already condemned who will not labor zealously for the state will only indulge their hope of escape.

sentences.zh: 且如以兵代之，兵若以不能力田為辭，則將移內地之民耕邊塞之地乎？

translations.literal: moreover, if soldiers are substituted in their place, and soldiers plead inability to till the fields, are inland people then to be moved to farm the borderlands?
translations.idiomatic: And if troops take their place, what when soldiers plead they cannot farm—shall inland peasants be shifted to till the frontier instead?

sentences.zh: 此事之斷不可行者。

translations.literal: This is something that absolutely cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: That course is utterly out of the question.

sentences.zh: 海望心地純良，但識見平常，所奏豈可盡以為是？

translations.literal: Hai Wang's heart is pure and good, but his judgment is ordinary; how can everything he memorializes be taken as correct?
translations.idiomatic: Hai Wang is honest in heart but commonplace in judgment; not everything he urges should be accepted.

sentences.zh: 議覆觀望游移，後當以此為戒。

translations.literal: In replying to deliberations he shows hesitation and vacillation; hereafter let this be a warning.
translations.idiomatic: His replies to council debate waver and hedge—let that be a lesson hereafter.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，泰陵工成，授拖沙喇哈番世職。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, when the Tailing works were completed, he was granted the hereditary rank of Tashalahafan.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2, after the Tailing mausoleum was finished, he received the hereditary rank of Tashalahafan.

sentences.zh: 尋罷總理事務處，復設辦理軍機處，海望仍為辦理軍機大臣。

translations.literal: Soon the General Affairs Office was abolished and the Grand Council was re-established; Hai Wang remained a Grand Council minister.
translations.idiomatic: The General Affairs Office was soon abolished and the Grand Council restored; Hai Wang stayed on as a council minister.

sentences.zh: 敘勞，復加拖沙喇哈番世職。

translations.literal: For recorded merit, he was again granted an additional Tashalahafan hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: His services were rewarded with a second Tashalahafan hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 四年，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was given the title Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 初，上命停捐例，廷臣議但留收穀捐監，俾各省積穀備荒。

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor had ordered an end to purchase-of-office regulations; the court ministers deliberated but to retain grain-donation purchase of supervisory rank, so that the provinces might store grain against famine.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the throne had halted the sale of offices; ministers argued to keep only the grain-donation route to supervisory rank so provinces could build famine reserves.

sentences.zh: 六年，御史趙青藜請並停之，復下廷臣議，請仍其舊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Censor Zhao Qingli asked that this too be stopped; the matter was again referred to the court ministers, who asked to keep the old practice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Censor Zhao Qingli urged abolishing that as well; ministers were consulted again and asked to leave the system unchanged.

sentences.zh: 海望奏：「外省收捐繁難，原議各省捐貯穀數三千餘萬石，今報部者僅二百五十餘萬石，不足十之一。

translations.literal: Hai Wang memorialized: "Collecting donations in the outer provinces is cumbersome and difficult; it was originally planned that the provinces would donate and store more than thirty million piculs of grain, yet what has been reported to the ministry is only a little over 2.5 million piculs—less than one-tenth.
translations.idiomatic: Hai Wang memorialized that provincial grain donations were hard to collect: the original plan called for more than thirty million piculs stored in the provinces, yet reports to the ministry showed barely 2.5 million—less than a tenth.

sentences.zh: 不若停各省捐穀，令在部交銀，轉撥各省買穀，俟倉貯充盈，請旨停止。

translations.literal: It would be better to stop provincial grain donations, require payment in silver at the ministry, and allocate funds to the provinces to buy grain; when granary stores are full, then request an imperial order to stop.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed ending provincial grain donations, taking silver at the ministry, and remitting it for provincial purchases, then seeking leave to halt once the granaries were truly full.

sentences.zh: 」上命在部交銀，在外交穀，聽士民之便。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered that silver be paid at the ministry and grain paid in the provinces, according to what was convenient for scholars and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ruled: pay silver in the capital or grain in the provinces, whichever suited donors.

sentences.zh: 諭謂：「地方積穀不厭其多，賑恤加恩，亦所時有，正未易言倉貯充盈也。

translations.literal: The instruction said: "Local grain reserves can never be too great; relief and added grace are also frequent; it is truly not easy to say that granary stores are already full.
translations.idiomatic: He added that local reserves could never be too large, that relief and special grace were frequent, and that one could hardly speak of granaries already being full.

sentences.zh: 海望久充崇文門監督，御史胡定奏言：「崇文門徵稅，有掛錘、頂秤諸名，百斤作百四五十斤。

translations.literal: Hai Wang had long served as Supervisor of Chongwen Gate; Censor Hu Ding memorialized: "At Chongwen Gate in collecting taxes there are names such as 'hanging weight' and 'topping the scale,' so that a hundred jin are reckoned as one hundred forty or fifty jin.
translations.idiomatic: Hai Wang had long overseen Chongwen Gate. Censor Hu Ding reported that its collectors used tricks called "hanging weight" and "topping the scale," turning a hundred jin into one hundred forty or fifty.

sentences.zh: 稅額雖未增，實已加數倍。

translations.literal: Though the tax quota was not increased, in fact it had been multiplied several times.
translations.idiomatic: The statutory levy had not risen, yet the take had multiplied several times over.

sentences.zh: 雜物自各門入，恣意需索，更數倍於稅額。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous goods entering through the various gates were extorted at will, several times more than the tax quota.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous goods admitted through other gates were squeezed for arbitrary fees many times the tax itself.

sentences.zh: 外省各關，如杭州北新關，自南而北十餘裡，稽察乃有七處，留難苛索，百倍於物價。

translations.literal: At outer-province passes, such as Hangzhou's Beixin Pass, for more than ten li from south to north there were seven inspection points, detaining and extorting at a hundred times the value of the goods.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial customs were worse—for example Hangzhou's Beixin Pass, where over ten li of road had seven checkpoints, with delays and exactions reaching a hundredfold the goods' worth.

sentences.zh: 蓋由官吏務欲稅課浮於舊額，吏胥藉得恣睢無忌，請敕嚴禁。

translations.literal: This was because officials strove to make tax receipts exceed the old quotas, and clerks took the chance to act lawlessly without restraint; he asked that an imperial order strictly forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were pressing revenue above old quotas, and clerks used the chance to extort without restraint; he begged a stern imperial prohibition.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「海望領崇文門稅務，侭收侭解，盡行入官，因而見其獨多。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Hai Wang oversaw Chongwen Gate tax affairs; whatever was collected was fully remitted to the treasury, and therefore his receipts alone appear large.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "Hai Wang ran Chongwen Gate taxes—whatever came in went straight to the treasury, so his totals look large.

sentences.zh: 如定所奏，種種苛索，朕信其必無。

translations.literal: As for what Ding memorialized—every sort of harsh exaction—I am confident there was none.
translations.idiomatic: The abuses Ding describes, I am sure, did not occur under him.

sentences.zh: 外省關課，應令督撫嚴察。

translations.literal: Outer-province customs revenue should be ordered to the governors-general and governors for strict inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial customs are for governors-general and governors to investigate strictly.

sentences.zh: 」海望旋調禮部尚書。

translations.literal: " Hai Wang was soon transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: " Hai Wang was soon transferred to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十年，上以海望精力漸衰，罷辦理軍機。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, because the Emperor saw that Hai Wang's vigor was gradually declining, he dismissed him from handling military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Emperor judged Hai Wang's strength was failing and removed him from the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十四年，復調戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was again transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was transferred back to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以建築兩郊壇宇發帑過多，與侍郎三和等自行奏請嚴議，當奪官，上寬之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, because building the altar compounds for the two suburban sacrifices had drawn excessively on the treasury, he together with Vice Minister Sanhe and others voluntarily memorialized requesting severe deliberation; the penalty should have been deprivation of office, but the Emperor was lenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, construction of the suburban altar compounds had drawn too heavily on the treasury; Hai Wang, Vice Minister Sanhe, and others jointly memorialized asking for strict discipline, an offense that normally meant dismissal—but the Emperor was merciful.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒，遣散秩大臣博爾木查奠茶酒，賜祭葬，諡勤恪。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died; a minister without fixed rank, Bor Mucha, was dispatched to offer tea and wine; funeral sacrifices and burial honors were granted, and the posthumous name Qinke was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twentieth year. The court sent Bor Mucha, a minister without fixed rank, to offer libations at the bier, granted state funeral rites, and posthumously named him Qinke, "Diligent and Respectful."

sentences.zh: 三和，納喇氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Sanhe, of the Nara clan, was a Bannerman of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Sanhe, of the Nara clan, came from the Manchu Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 初授護軍校，累遷一等侍衛。

translations.literal: He was first appointed bodyguard captain and was promoted repeatedly to first-class imperial bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a bodyguard captain and rose step by step to first-class imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六年，授總管內務府大臣，遷戶部侍郎，調工部，復調還戶部。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qianlong he was appointed Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department, promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, transferred to Works, and then transferred back to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 6 he became Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department, then Vice Minister of Revenue, then Works, and finally back to Revenue again.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 尋降授侍郎，調戶部，復調還工部。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was demoted to vice minister, transferred to Revenue, and again transferred back to Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was demoted to vice minister, shifted to Revenue, then shifted back to Works.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was appointed Grand Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he was named a Grand Minister.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，卒，賜祭葬，諡誠毅。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he died; funeral sacrifices and burial honors were granted, and the posthumous name Chengyi was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-eighth year; the court granted state funeral rites and posthumously named him Chengyi, "Sincere and Resolute."

sentences.zh: 莽鵠立，字樹本，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Mang Hulu, styled Shuben, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Mang Hulu, courtesy name Shuben, was of the Irgen Gioro clan and the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 曾祖富拉塔，居葉赫，天聰時來歸，隸蒙古正藍旗。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Fu Lata lived at Yehe; he came over and submitted during the Tiancong period and was attached to the Mongol Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Fu Lata had lived at Yehe and submitted during the Tiancong reign, after which he was enrolled in the Mongol Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 祖莽吉圖，從睿親王伐明，徇山東，圍錦州，擊敗洪承疇援兵；

translations.literal: His grandfather Mang Jitu followed Prince Rui in the campaign against the Ming, swept Shandong, besieged Jinzhou, and defeated the relief army of Hong Chengchou;
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mang Jitu followed Prince Rui in the war against the Ming, swept Shandong, laid siege to Jinzhou, and routed Hong Chengchou's relief force;

sentences.zh: 入關逐李自成至慶都；

translations.literal: after entering the pass he pursued Li Zicheng to Qingdu;
translations.idiomatic: after the Manchus entered the pass he pursued Li Zicheng as far as Qingdu;

sentences.zh: 又從下雲南。

translations.literal: he then followed in the conquest of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: and then took part in the subjugation of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 累擢正藍旗滿洲梅勒額真，授世職三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to meiren ejen of the Plain Blue Banner Manchus and was granted the hereditary office of third-class adaha commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to meiren ejen of the Plain Blue Banner Manchus and received the hereditary rank of third-class adaha commandant.

sentences.zh: 莽鵠立，事聖祖，初授理籓院筆帖式。

translations.literal: Mang Hulu served the Kangxi Emperor and was first appointed a clerk at the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Mang Hulu entered service under the Kangxi Emperor, first as a clerk in the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 累遷員外郎，迭充右翼監督、滸墅關監督。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to vice director, and in rotation served as superintendent of the Right Wing and superintendent of Husu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced through the ranks to vice director and in turn supervised the Right Wing and the Husu customs barrier.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，命協辦理籓院侍郎，旋擢御史。

translations.literal: When Yongzheng acceded, he was ordered to assist as Vice Minister at the Court of Colonial Affairs and was soon promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongzheng's accession he was ordered to assist as vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and soon after was raised to censor.

sentences.zh: 莽鵠立精繪事，令恭繪聖祖御容。

translations.literal: Mang Hulu was skilled in painting and was ordered to paint respectfully the imperial portrait of the Kangxi Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Mang Hulu excelled at painting and was commanded to render a reverent portrait of the Kangxi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，改入滿洲，以本族別編佐領，俾莽鵠立世管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was transferred to Manchu status; a separate assistant commandant's company was constituted within his clan for Mang Hulu to hold in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he was re-registered as Manchu; a separate assistant commandant's company was carved out of his lineage for Mang Hulu's family to hold in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 出巡長蘆鹽政，疏言：「長蘆諸商行鹽地，有額引不能銷者，有額外多銷者。

translations.literal: When sent on inspection tour of the Changlu salt administration, he memorialized: "In the districts through which Changlu merchants carry salt, some have quota certificates that cannot be sold through, while in others sales exceed the quota.
translations.idiomatic: On tour as Changlu salt controller he memorialized: "Among the districts where Changlu merchants peddle salt, some cannot sell through their allotted certificates, while others sell far beyond quota.

sentences.zh: 請通融運銷，量增引目。

translations.literal: He requested flexible transport and marketing and a measured increase in certificate quotas.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that transport and sales be flexibly coordinated and certificate quotas increased in due measure.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved it.

sentences.zh: 二年，疏請元年積引寬限分銷，部議不允，再疏請，特許之。

translations.literal: In the second year he memorialized requesting that accumulated certificates from the first year be granted an extended deadline for phased distribution; the ministry deliberated and did not permit it; he memorialized again and was specially permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he asked that unsold certificates from year one be given a longer deadline for staggered distribution; the ministry refused, but after a second memorial the Emperor granted it by special edict.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「山東加增引目，州縣多寡不均。

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "Shandong's added certificate quotas are unevenly distributed among prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: "The extra certificate quotas in Shandong are unevenly apportioned among prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 請減多增寡，以甦商困。

translations.literal: He requested reducing where there is excess and increasing where there is little, to relieve merchants' distress.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed cutting quotas where they were too large and raising them where they were too small, to ease the merchants' hardship.

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「增復引目，視現辦商人按名均分。

translations.literal: " He again memorialized: "When restoring increased certificate quotas, they should be divided equally by name among the merchants presently handling the trade.
translations.idiomatic: Another memorial read: "Any restored quota should be divided evenly, merchant by merchant, among those currently licensed to trade.

sentences.zh: 」上允之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 三年，疏言：「山東灶丁，遵康熙五十二年恩詔，審丁不加賦。

translations.literal: In the third year he memorialized: "Shandong salt-pan households, in accord with the grace edict of the fifty-second year of Kangxi, should have their household rolls reviewed without added tax.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he wrote: "Shandong salt-pan households, under Kangxi's grace edict of year fifty-two, ought to have their household registers reviewed without extra levy.

sentences.zh: 」下部議行。

translations.literal: " It was sent to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The court referred it to the ministries for enactment.

sentences.zh: 又疏請清察灶地，敕直隸、山東督撫遣員清丈。

translations.literal: He again memorialized requesting a thorough survey of salt-pan lands; an edict ordered the governors-general and governors of Zhili and Shandong to dispatch officers to measure and clear the registers.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for a full audit of salt-pan lands; the throne ordered the Zhili and Shandong governors-general and governors to send officials to survey and register them.

sentences.zh: 遷大理寺卿，再遷兵部侍郎，領鹽政如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to President of the Court of Judicial Review, then again to Vice Minister of War, while continuing to head the salt administration as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made president of the Court of Judicial Review, then vice minister of War, while retaining charge of the salt administration.

sentences.zh: 天津改衛為州，初議隸河間府。

translations.literal: When Tianjin was changed from a guard to a prefecture, the initial plan was to place it under Hejian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianjin was elevated from guard to prefecture, the first proposal made it a dependency of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 莽鵠立請改為直隸州，以武清、靜海、青縣屬焉。

translations.literal: Mang Hulu requested that it be made a directly controlled prefecture, with Wuqing, Jinghai, and Qing Counties placed under it.
translations.idiomatic: Mang Hulu urged that it be made a directly controlled prefecture subordinate to the province, with Wuqing, Jinghai, and Qing attached to its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 並丁入地議起，莽鵠立以山東灶丁丁多地少，請以其半入地，其半仍按丁徵賦。

translations.literal: When debate arose over merging household quotas into land tax, Mang Hulu, on the grounds that Shandong salt-pan households had many men but little land, requested that half be folded into land tax and half still levied by household.
translations.idiomatic: When the policy of merging household quotas into land tax came up for debate, Mang Hulu argued that Shandong salt households had too many men on too little land and asked that half the levy shift to land tax while half remain assessed per household.

sentences.zh: 下部議，從之。

translations.literal: It was sent to the ministry for deliberation and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal went to the ministries and was adopted.

sentences.zh: 四年，以御史顧琮巡視鹽政，仍命莽鵠立監理。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, because Censor Gu Cong was sent to inspect the salt administration, Mang Hulu was still ordered to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Censor Gu Cong was dispatched to inspect salt affairs, Mang Hulu was still ordered to oversee the office.

sentences.zh: 尋調禮部，令與顧琮監造天津水師營房，工久未竣，上以責莽鵠立，調刑部，召還京。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites and ordered together with Gu Cong to supervise construction of the Tianjin naval garrison barracks; because the work was long unfinished the Emperor blamed Mang Hulu, transferred him to Punishments, and recalled him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to Rites and told to build the Tianjin naval barracks alongside Gu Cong; when the project dragged on the Emperor held Mang Hulu responsible, shifted him to Punishments, and summoned him back to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 五年，復調禮部，仍署長蘆鹽政。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was again transferred to Rites and continued to hold the Changlu salt post on an acting basis.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he returned to Rites while again acting as Changlu salt controller.

sentences.zh: 授甘肅巡撫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 六年，師入西藏，諭莽鵠立赴西寧料理。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when the army entered Tibet, he was instructed to proceed to Xining to manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, as troops marched into Tibet, he was told to go to Xining and manage logistics.

sentences.zh: 西寧道劉之珍等誤軍興，總督岳鍾琪疏劾，上以責莽鵠立，解巡撫，召還京。

translations.literal: Liu Zhizhen of the Xining circuit and others mishandled military provisioning; Governor-General Yue Zhongqi memorialized in impeachment; the Emperor blamed Mang Hulu, relieved him of the governorship, and recalled him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhizhen of the Xining circuit and others botched army supply; Governor-General Yue Zhongqi impeached them, and the Emperor faulted Mang Hulu as well, stripped him of the governorship, and recalled him to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 署正藍旗滿洲副都統，兼管理籓院侍郎。

translations.literal: He served in acting capacity as Vice Commander of the Plain Blue Banner Manchus and concurrently as Vice Minister managing the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He acted as vice commander of the Plain Blue Banner Manchus while concurrently managing vice-ministerial duties at the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢正藍旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Commander of the Plain Blue Banner Mongols.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made commander of the Plain Blue Mongol Banner.

sentences.zh: 八年，命協同辦理直隸水利營田。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to assist jointly in managing Zhili waterworks and military colony fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was ordered to help administer Zhili's water conservancy and garrison farming colonies.

sentences.zh: 十年，調鑲白旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Commander of the Bordered White Banner Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to commander of the Bordered White Banner Manchus.

sentences.zh: 十三年，與都統襲英誠公豐盛額並命辦理軍機事務。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he and Commander Fengshen'e, who had inherited the title Duke Yingcheng, were jointly ordered to handle military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he and Fengshen'e, commander and inheritor of the dukedom of Yingcheng, were both appointed to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，改設總理事務處，莽鵠立與豐盛額罷直回本任。

translations.literal: When Qianlong acceded, the General Affairs Office was established anew; Mang Hulu and Fengshen'e were dismissed from daily attendance and returned to their original posts.
translations.idiomatic: At Qianlong's accession the General Affairs Office was reorganized; Mang Hulu and Fengshen'e left daily council duty and resumed their regular posts.

sentences.zh: 尋署工部尚書，又調正藍旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed acting Minister of Works, then transferred to Commander of the Plain Blue Banner Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting minister of works, then transferred to commander of the Plain Blue Manchu Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，卒，賜祭葬，諡勤敏。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he died; sacrificial rites at burial were granted, and the posthumous name Qinmin was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Qianlong (1736); the court granted funeral sacrifices and gave him the posthumous name Qinmin, "Diligent and Keen."

sentences.zh: 杭奕祿，完顏氏，滿洲鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Hang Yilu, of the Wanyan clan, was a Bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Hang Yilu, of the Wanyan clan, came from the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 初授中書。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed a Secretariat draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a secretariat draftsman.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，授額外員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was appointed a supernumerary vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng's first year he received a supernumerary vice-directorship.

sentences.zh: 未幾，補御史，即遷光祿寺少卿。

translations.literal: Before long he was made a censor and at once was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he became a censor and was promptly promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made director of the same court.

sentences.zh: 上蠲蘇州、松江田賦四十五萬，杭奕祿疏言：「此為未有殊恩。

translations.literal: The Emperor remitted 450,000 taels of Suzhou and Songjiang land tax; Hang Yilu memorialized: "This is an unprecedented special grace.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne remitted 450,000 taels of land tax for Suzhou and Songjiang, Hang Yilu memorialized: "This is a favor without precedent.

sentences.zh: 有田納賦，既邀蠲免；

translations.literal: Those who own land and pay tax have already received remission;
translations.idiomatic: Landowners who pay the land tax have already gained exemption;

sentences.zh: 無田而佃種人田者，納租業主，亦宜酌減，俾貧富均霑實惠。

translations.literal: those who own no land but tenant others' fields and pay rent to landlords should also have reductions weighed, so that rich and poor alike may share the real benefit."
translations.idiomatic: tenants who farm another's land and pay rent to the proprietor should also receive a measured reduction, so rich and poor alike may share the real benefit."

sentences.zh: 」上謂此奏甚公，下廷臣議，定業戶免額一錢，佃戶免租穀三升。

translations.literal: The Emperor said this memorial was very fair, referred it to the court ministers, and they fixed exemption of one mace of quota for proprietor households and three sheng of rent grain for tenant households.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor called the memorial admirably fair and sent it to the ministries; they set a one-mace quota cut for proprietor households and a three-sheng rent-grain cut for tenants.

sentences.zh: 上命如議速行。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered that it be carried out swiftly as deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the measure implemented at once.

sentences.zh: 擢左副都御史，仍兼管光祿寺。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief while still concurrently managing the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to left vice censor-in-chief while keeping charge of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 五年，命與內閣學士任蘭枝使安南宣諭。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was ordered, together with Grand Secretariat Academician Ren Lanzhi, to go as envoy to Annan to proclaim the imperial message.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he and Grand Secretariat academician Ren Lanzhi were sent to Annan as imperial envoys.

sentences.zh: 初，雲南總督高其倬奏安南國界有百二十里舊屬內地，應​​以賭咒河為界，安南國王黎維祹奏辯。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yunnan Governor-General Gao Qizuo had memorialized that 120 li of the Annan border had formerly belonged to the interior and the boundary should be the Duzhou River; King Le Weizuo of Annan memorialized in rebuttal.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yunnan governor-general Gao Qizuo had argued that 120 li along the Annan frontier had once been imperial territory and that the border should run along the Duzhou River; King Le Weizuo of Annan replied in protest.

sentences.zh: 上命雲貴總督鄂爾泰覆覈，予地八十里，以鉛廠山下小河內四十里為界，維祹復奏辯。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Ortai to re-examine the case, granted 80 li of territory, and set the border at forty li within the small river below Lead Mine Mountain; Weizuo again memorialized in rebuttal.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general Ortai to reinvestigate; Ortai awarded eighty li and drew the line forty li inside the stream below Lead Mine Mountain—whereupon Weizuo protested again.

sentences.zh: 上敕維祹毋以侵占內地為嫌，疑懼申辯。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed Weizuo not to worry that he was accused of encroaching on interior territory and to cease pleading out of suspicion and fear.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Weizuo not to take alarm at the charge of encroachment and to stop defending himself out of fear.

sentences.zh: 至是，復命杭奕祿等往​​諭意，未至，維祹上表謝罪。

translations.literal: At this time he again ordered Hang Yilu and others to go proclaim the imperial intent; before they arrived, Weizuo submitted a memorial asking forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Now the court again dispatched Hang Yilu and his party to explain the imperial mind; before they arrived, Weizuo submitted a memorial of repentance.

sentences.zh: 六年，命鄂爾泰以鉛廠山下地四十里予安南，別頒敕命杭奕祿等齎往宣諭。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he ordered Ortai to give Annan the forty li of land below Lead Mine Mountain, and separately issued an edict ordering Hang Yilu and others to carry it and go proclaim.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Ortai was ordered to yield the forty li below Lead Mine Mountain to Annan, and a separate edict was issued for Hang Yilu and his colleagues to carry abroad.

sentences.zh: 杭奕祿至鎮南關，維祹使出關迎。

translations.literal: When Hang Yilu reached Zhennan Pass, Weizuo sent men out of the pass to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhennan Pass, Weizuo sent officials beyond the gate to receive him.

sentences.zh: 進次貂瑤營，維祹復使迎勞，請儀注，議行其國禮，五拜三叩。

translations.literal: Advancing to camp at Diaoyao, Weizuo again sent men to welcome and entertain him, requesting ritual protocol; after discussion they decided to follow Annan's court ritual—five bows and three prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: Moving on to Diaoyao camp, Weizuo again sent a welcoming party and asked about ceremony; after debate they agreed on Annan court ritual—five bows and three kowtows.

sentences.zh: 杭奕祿等持不可，乃請聽命。

translations.literal: Hang Yilu and the others held that this could not be done, so they requested to hear the imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: Hang Yilu and his colleagues objected and asked to await the throne's decision.

sentences.zh: 渡富良江至長安門，維祹跪迎。

translations.literal: Crossing the Fu River to Chang'an Gate, Weizuo knelt to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Fu River to Chang'an Gate, where Weizuo knelt to greet them.

sentences.zh: 杭奕祿等捧敕入自中門，維祹率將吏等聽宣敕，敕曰：「朕前令守土各官清理疆界，未及於安南也。

translations.literal: Hang Yilu and the others bore the edict in through the central gate; Weizuo led his generals and officials to hear the edict proclaimed. The edict read: "We previously ordered each frontier official to clear territorial boundaries, but this had not yet reached Annan.
translations.idiomatic: Hang Yilu and the others entered by the central gate bearing the edict; Weizuo gathered his commanders and officials to hear it read. The edict ran: "We earlier ordered frontier officials to survey borders, but Annan had not yet been included.

sentences.zh: 總督高其倬職任封疆，考​​志乘，訪輿論，知開化府與安南分界當在逢春里之賭咒河，乃奏聞設汛。

translations.literal: Governor Gao Qizuo, charged with guarding the frontier, examined local gazetteers and sought public opinion, and knew that the border between Kaihua Prefecture and Annan ought to lie at the Duzhou River in Fengchunli; he therefore memorialized and reported and established garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Gao Qizuo, charged with the frontier, studied gazetteers and local opinion and concluded that Kaihua prefecture and Annan should be divided at the Duzhou River in Fengchunli; he memorialized accordingly and proposed garrison posts.

sentences.zh: 王疏陳，復命總督鄂爾泰秉公辦理。

translations.literal: The King memorialized in detail; We again ordered Governor Ortai to handle the matter impartially.
translations.idiomatic: The king replied at length; We then ordered Governor Ortai to settle the matter impartially.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰體朕懷遠之心，定界於鉛廠山下小河，縮地八十里。

translations.literal: Ortai, taking to heart Our mind of cherishing those afar, fixed the border at the small river below Lead Mine Mountain, shrinking the territory by eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: Ortai, honoring Our wish to cherish distant peoples, drew the line at the stream below Lead Mine Mountain and ceded eighty li.

sentences.zh: 誠為仁至義盡，此皆地方大臣職分所當為。

translations.literal: It was truly benevolence carried to its limit and righteousness fulfilled—all of this is what frontier great officials should do in the course of duty.
translations.idiomatic: This was benevolence and righteousness pushed to their limit—precisely what a frontier minister owes his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 朕統馭寰區，凡屬臣服之邦，皆隸版籍。

translations.literal: We govern the whole realm; every state that submits is entered in Our registers.
translations.idiomatic: We rule the entire realm; every submitting state is recorded in Our registers.

sentences.zh: 安南既列籓封，尺地莫非吾土，何必較論此區區四十里之地？

translations.literal: Annan is already listed among the feudatories—every foot of ground is Our soil; why argue over this mere forty li?
translations.idiomatic: Annan already ranks among Our feudatories—every inch is imperial soil; why quarrel over a mere forty li?

sentences.zh: 若王以至情懇求，朕何難開恩賜與？

translations.literal: If the King earnestly beseeches Us with utmost sincerity, how hard would it be for Us to open grace and grant it?
translations.idiomatic: Had the king pleaded with sincere feeling, how difficult would it have been for Us to grant it in grace?

sentences.zh: 祗以兩督臣定界時，王激切奏請，過於觖望，失事上之禮，朕亦無從施惠。

translations.literal: Only because when the two governors fixed the border the King urgently and repeatedly memorialized, overstepping in expectation, and failed in the proper deference owed a sovereign—We also had no way to show favor.
translations.idiomatic: But when the two governors drew the line, the king's urgent, repeated petitions pressed too hard and breached the deference owed a sovereign—so We could not show favor.

sentences.zh: 頃鄂爾泰以王本章呈奏，詞意虔恭。

translations.literal: Recently Ortai presented the King's latest memorial; the wording was reverent and respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Ortai has lately forwarded the king's new memorial, and its tone is reverent.

sentences.zh: 王既知盡禮，朕自可加恩，將此地仍賜王世守，並遣大臣前往宣諭。

translations.literal: Since the King now knows how to observe full propriety, We can naturally add grace, grant this territory again for the King's house to hold in perpetuity, and send great ministers to go proclaim the message.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the king understands full propriety, We may extend grace, restore this land for his house to hold forever, and send great ministers to proclaim Our will.

sentences.zh: 王其知朕意！

translations.literal: Let the King understand Our intent!
translations.idiomatic: Let the king take Our meaning to heart!

sentences.zh: 」宣畢，維祹行三跪九叩禮。

translations.literal: When the proclamation was finished, Weizuo performed the three kneelings and nine knockings of the head.
translations.idiomatic: When the reading ended, Weizuo performed the three kneelings and nine kowtows.

sentences.zh: 杭奕祿等復宣諭恩德，維祹誓世世子孫永矢臣節。

translations.literal: Hang Yilu and the others again proclaimed imperial grace; Weizuo swore that his sons and grandsons for generations would forever uphold their duty as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Hang Yilu and his party then proclaimed the throne's grace again; Weizuo swore that his line would forever keep faith as subjects.

sentences.zh: 杭奕祿等使還，維祹送至長安門，餽贐杭奕祿等，不受。

translations.literal: When Hang Yilu and the others returned as envoys, Weizuo saw them off to Chang'an Gate and presented farewell gifts to Hang Yilu and the others, which they declined.
translations.idiomatic: On their return, Weizuo escorted them to Chang'an Gate and offered parting gifts, which they refused.

sentences.zh: 至鎮南關，維祹使齎謝表請轉奏。

translations.literal: At Zhennan Pass, Weizuo sent men bearing a memorial of thanks and asked that it be forwarded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhennan Pass he sent bearers with a memorial of thanks, asking that it be relayed to the throne.

sentences.zh: 杭奕祿等還京師，疏聞，請宣付史館，允之。

translations.literal: Hang Yilu and the others returned to the capital, reported in a memorial, and asked that the proclamation be copied for the Historiography Office; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Beijing, Hang Yilu and his colleagues reported by memorial and asked that the edict be entered in the Historiography Office; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 授刑部侍郎，署吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Punishments and acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice minister of punishments and acting minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 六年，湖南靖州諸生曾靜遣其徒張熙變姓名投書川陝總督岳鍾琪，略言清為金裔，鍾琪乃鄂王后，勸令復金、宋之仇，同謀舉事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Zeng Jing, a licentiate of Jingzhou in Hunan, sent his disciple Zhang Xi, who changed his name, to deliver a letter to Sichuan-Shaanxi Governor-General Yue Zhongqi, briefly stating that the Qing were descendants of the Jin, that Zhongqi was a descendant of the house of E, and urging him to avenge the Jin and Song, and to conspire together to raise an uprising.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Zeng Jing, a licentiate from Jingzhou in Hunan, sent his student Zhang Xi—traveling under a false name—to Yue Zhongqi, governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi. The letter claimed the Qing were heirs of the Jin, that Zhongqi descended from the house of Prince E, and urged him to settle old scores with Jin and Song and join a rising.

sentences.zh: 鍾琪大駭，鞫熙，熙不肯言其實；

translations.literal: Zhongqi was greatly alarmed and interrogated Xi; Xi refused to speak the truth;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqi was appalled and questioned Xi, but Xi would not confess;

sentences.zh: 乃置熙密室，陽與誓，將迎其師與謀，始得熙及靜姓名，奏​​聞。

translations.literal: he then placed Xi in a secret chamber, pretended to swear an oath with him, and said he would welcome Xi's teacher to plot together; only then did he obtain the names of Xi and Jing, and memorialized to report.
translations.idiomatic: so he shut Xi in a private room, feigned a pact, and promised to welcome Xi's teacher to plot—only then learning the names of Xi and Jing, which he reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上命杭奕祿及副都統覺羅海蘭如湖南，會巡撫王國棟捕靜嚴鞫。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Hang Yilu and Vice Commander Jueluo Hailan to go to Hunan, join Governor Wang Guodong in arresting Jing, and conduct a strict interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Hang Yilu and vice commander Jueluo Hailan to Hunan to join Governor Wang Guodong in seizing Jing and examining him under torture.

sentences.zh: 靜言因讀呂留良評選時文論夷、夏語激烈，遣熙求得留良遺書，與留良子毅中，及其弟子嚴鴻逵，鴻逵弟子沈在寬等往還，沈溺其說，妄生異心。

translations.literal: Jing said that through reading Lü Liuliang's annotated examination essays, where discourse on Yi and Xia was vehement, he had sent Xi to obtain Liuliang's posthumous writings; he corresponded with Liuliang's son Yizhong, his disciple Yan Hongkui, Hongkui's disciple Shen Zaikuan, and others, became steeped in their doctrine, and rashly harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said he had read Lü Liuliang's annotated examination essays, with their fierce Yi–Xia rhetoric, and sent Xi to obtain Liuliang's posthumous works; he exchanged letters with Liuliang's son Yizhong, his disciple Yan Hongkui, Hongkui's student Shen Zaikuan, and others, drowned himself in their teaching, and let a treasonous mind take root.

sentences.zh: 留良，浙江石門諸生，康熙初講學負盛名，時已前死。

translations.literal: Liuliang was a licentiate of Shimen in Zhejiang, famous in the early Kangxi period for his lecturing; by then he had long been dead.
translations.idiomatic: Liuliang had been a Shimen licentiate in Zhejiang, renowned in early Kangxi for his teaching, but was already long dead.

sentences.zh: 上命逮靜、熙、毅中、鴻逵、在寬等至京師。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Jing, Xi, Yizhong, Hongkui, Zaikuan, and the others arrested and brought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Jing, Xi, Yizhong, Hongkui, Zaikuan, and the rest arrested and brought to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 靜至，廷鞫，自承迂妄，為留良所誤，手書供辭，盛稱上恩德。

translations.literal: When Jing arrived, he was interrogated at court; he confessed of his own accord that he had been perverse and reckless and misled by Liuliang, wrote out his confession in his own hand, and lavishly praised the Emperor's grace and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing arrived he was examined at court; he admitted his folly, blamed Liuliang for misleading him, wrote a confession in his own hand, and poured praise on the Emperor's grace.

sentences.zh: 上命編次為大義覺迷錄，令杭奕祿以靜至江寧、杭州、蘇州宣講。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered it compiled as Record of the Great Meaning for Awakening the Deluded, and ordered Hang Yilu to go to Jiangning, Hangzhou, and Suzhou to lecture on it with Jing in tow.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had the case compiled as the Record of the Great Meaning for Awakening the Deluded and sent Hang Yilu to lecture on it in Jiangning, Hangzhou, and Suzhou—with Jing brought along.

sentences.zh: 事畢，命並熙釋勿誅，戮留良屍，誅毅中並鴻逵、在寬等，戍留良諸子孫。

translations.literal: When the affair was concluded, he ordered Zeng Jing and Zhang Xi released and not executed, exposed Lü Liuliang's corpse, executed Yi Zhong together with Hong Kui, Zai Kuan, and others, and banished Lü's descendants to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was closed, the Emperor spared Zeng Jing and Zhang Xi, had Lü Liuliang's corpse dismembered and displayed, put Yi Zhong, Hong Kui, Zai Kuan, and the rest to death, and sent Lü's kin into exile.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，乃命誅靜、熙。

translations.literal: When Qianlong acceded, he then ordered Jing and Xi executed.
translations.idiomatic: After Qianlong took the throne, he had Jing and Xi put to death.

sentences.zh: 七年，授杭奕祿鑲紅旗滿洲副都統。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Hang Yilu was appointed Vice Commander of the Bordered Red Banner Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made vice commander of the Bordered Red Manchu Banner.

sentences.zh: 八年，命解部事，尋复補禮部侍郎，署前鋒統領。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to relinquish his ministry duties; soon afterward he was again appointed Vice Minister of Rites and served in acting capacity as commander of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was relieved of his ministry post, then soon reappointed vice minister of Rites and acting vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 上命杭奕祿偕侍郎眾佛保宣諭準噶爾。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Hang Yilu together with Vice Minister Zhongfobao to proclaim an imperial message to the Dzungars.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Hang Yilu and Vice Minister Zhongfobao to announce the court's will to the Dzungars.

sentences.zh: 九年，師徵準噶爾，上慮陝、甘民或以用兵為累，命杭奕祿與左都御史史貽直、署內務府總管鄭渾寶，率庶吉士、六部學習主事、國子監肄​​業拔貢生等宣諭化導。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, as the army campaigned against the Dzungars, the Emperor feared the people of Shaanxi and Gansu might regard the war as a burden; he ordered Hang Yilu, together with Left Censor-in-Chief Shi Yizhi and Acting Grand Steward of the Imperial Household Zheng Hunbao, to lead licentiates of the Hanlin Academy, probationary directors from the Six Ministries, advanced students and tribute scholars from the Imperial Academy, and the like to proclaim and guide them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, with troops marching on the Dzungars, the Emperor worried that Shaanxi and Gansu might feel the strain of war. He sent Hang Yilu, Left Censor-in-Chief Shi Yizhi, and acting grand steward Zheng Hunbao, together with Hanlin licentiates, ministry trainees, and Imperial Academy students selected for advancement, to explain policy and reassure the people.

sentences.zh: 尋命杭奕祿協辦軍需。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Hang Yilu was ordered to assist in managing military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon put in charge of assisting with army logistics.

sentences.zh: 十年，命署西安將軍，授欽差大臣，察閱甘、涼及山西近邊營伍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered to serve as acting General at Xi'an, appointed Imperial Commissioner, and to inspect the garrisons of Ganzhou, Liangzhou, and the nearby border districts of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he acted as Xi'an general, received an imperial commission, and inspected troops in Ganzhou, Liangzhou, and Shanxi's frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 十一年，諭責杭奕祿驕奢放​​縱，擾累兵民，奪官，在肅州荷校。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year an edict rebuked Hang Yilu for arrogance, extravagance, and license, and for harassing soldiers and civilians; his office was stripped and he wore the cangue at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the throne denounced his arrogance and excess, his abuse of troops and civilians, stripped his rank, and had him pilloried at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，召至京師，授額外內閣學士，補工部侍郎，充世宗實錄副總裁。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was summoned to the capital, appointed an extra Grand Secretariat academician, restored as Vice Minister of Works, and made a deputy chief compiler of the Veritable Records of the Shizong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 he was recalled to Beijing, made an extra Grand Secretariat academician and vice minister of Works, and named deputy compiler of the Yongzheng Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 遣駐西藏辦事。

translations.literal: He was dispatched to serve as resident commissioner in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Tibet as resident commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，奏言：「西藏西南三千里外巴爾布國有三汗：一曰庫庫木，一曰顏布，一曰葉楞，雍正十一年嘗通貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he memorialized: "Three thousand li southwest of Tibet lies the state of Balbu, ruled by three khans: one named Kukumu, one Yanbu, and one Yeleng; in the eleventh year of Yongzheng they once sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he reported: "Three thousand li southwest of Tibet lies Balbu, with three khans—Kukumu, Yanbu, and Yeleng—who had sent tribute in Yongzheng 11.

sentences.zh: 近三汗交惡，貝勒頗羅鼐宣諭罷兵，三汗聽命，使呈進部落戶口數，並貢金銀、絲緞、珊瑚、念珠諸物。

translations.literal: Recently the three khans fell into mutual enmity; Beile Poluonai proclaimed an edict ordering them to cease fighting; the three khans obeyed, and were made to submit the population figures of their tribes, together with tribute of gold, silver, silk, coral, prayer beads, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the three khans had quarreled; Beile Poluonai announced an imperial message bidding them stop fighting. They obeyed, submitted tribal household registers, and sent tribute of gold, silver, silk, coral, rosaries, and the like.

sentences.zh: 」報聞。

translations.literal: " The report was received.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was noted.

sentences.zh: 尋召還，調刑部。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was recalled and transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and moved to Punishments.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢左都御史，列議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and enrolled among the Deliberative Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he rose to left censor-in-chief and took a seat among the deliberative ministers.

sentences.zh: 十年，以老乞休，諭留之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, citing age, he begged to retire; an edict ordered him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he asked to retire on grounds of age; the Emperor told him to stay.

sentences.zh: 十一年，上察其老憊，命致仕。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Emperor observed his aged weariness and ordered him to retire from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, seeing how worn he had grown, the Emperor let him retire.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year.

sentences.zh: 傅鼐，字閣峰，富察氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Fu Nai, courtesy name Gefeng, of the Fuca clan, was a Bannerman of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Nai, styled Gefeng, of the Fuca clan, came from the Manchu Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 初授侍衛。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed a guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a palace guardsman.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，授鑲黃旗漢軍副都統、兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng he was appointed Vice Commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner Chinese Martial and Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 he became vice commander of the Bordered Yellow Chinese Martial Banner and vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 三年，調盛京戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue at Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was moved to Mukden as vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 世宗在潛邸，夙知傅鼐好事，既即位，令隆科多察其為人。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yong was still in his private residence, he had long known Fu Nai to be meddlesome; once he acceded, he ordered Longkodo to observe his character.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng had known him as a busybody since his years in the princely mansion; on taking the throne he told Longkodo to look into the man.

sentences.zh: 隆科多稱傅鼐安靜。

translations.literal: Longkodo said Fu Nai was quiet and steady.
translations.idiomatic: Longkodo reported that Fu Nai was steady and restrained.

sentences.zh: 傅鼐在上前嘗言隆科多子岳興阿甚怨其父，謂「我家受恩深，當將生平行事據實奏聞，若稍有隱飾，罪更不可逭」。

translations.literal: Before the throne Fu Nai had once said that Longkodo's son Yue Xing'a bitterly resented his father, declaring, "Our house has received deep favor; we ought to report his conduct in life exactly as it was. If we conceal the least thing, the guilt will be all the harder to escape."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Nai had once told the Emperor that Yue Xing'a deeply resented his father Longkodo, saying, "Our family owes the throne too much to hide anything. Report his whole career truthfully—any concealment will only make the crime worse."

sentences.zh: 及隆科多被譴追贓，岳興阿隱其父財產。

translations.literal: When Longkodo was censured and pursued for restitution, Yue Xing'a concealed his father's property.
translations.idiomatic: When Longkodo fell under censure and was ordered to make restitution, Yue Xing'a hid his father's assets.

sentences.zh: 上以與傅鼐言不符，疑傅鼐與隆科多交結，慮且敗，預為岳興阿地。

translations.literal: Because this did not accord with what Fu Nai had said, the Emperor suspected Fu Nai of collusion with Longkodo, feared he might yet be exposed, and made room in advance for Yue Xing'a.
translations.idiomatic: This contradicted Fu Nai's account; the Emperor suspected collusion with Longkodo, feared exposure, and paved the way for Yue Xing'a instead.

sentences.zh: 會傅鼐任侍衛時，浙江糧道江國英被劾，為關說，得銀萬餘。

translations.literal: It happened that while Fu Nai was serving as guardsman, Jiang Guoying, grain intendant of Zhejiang, was impeached; Fu Nai intervened on his behalf and received more than ten thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: While he was still a guardsman, Zhejiang grain intendant Jiang Guoying was impeached; Fu Nai pulled strings for him and took more than ten thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 事發，上命奪官，械系逮詣京師，下刑部按治。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light, the Emperor ordered his office stripped, had him shackled and escorted to the capital, and handed him over to the Ministry of Punishments for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter broke, the Emperor stripped his rank, had him shackled and brought to Beijing, and sent him to the Ministry of Punishments for trial.

sentences.zh: 讞上，免死，發遣黑龍江。

translations.literal: When the finding was submitted, he was spared death and banished to Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict spared his life and sent him into exile at Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 九年，召還，赴大將軍馬爾賽軍營效力。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was recalled and sent to serve in the camp of the general-in-chief Ma'er Sai.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was recalled to serve on General-in-Chief Ma'er Sai's staff.

sentences.zh: 尋予侍郎銜，授參贊大臣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was granted the rank of vice minister and appointed a participating grand minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given vice-ministerial rank and made a participating grand minister.

sentences.zh: 十年，準噶爾台吉噶爾丹策零入寇，額駙策淩御之額爾德尼昭，噶爾丹策零大敗，自推河竄走。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Dzungar taiji Galdan Tseren invaded; the imperial son-in-law Ce Ling met him at Erdeneju, Galdan Tseren was utterly defeated, and fled in rout from the Tui River.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Dzungar taiji Galdan Tseren raided in force; Ce Ling, the emperor's son-in-law, met him at Erdeneju, shattered his army, and drove him fleeing along the Tui River.

sentences.zh: 時馬爾賽駐拜里城，有兵萬三千。

translations.literal: At that time Ma'er Sai was stationed at Baili city with thirteen thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Ma'er Sai then held Baili with thirteen thousand men.

sentences.zh: 策淩檄速發兵斷噶爾丹策零歸路，馬爾賽不能用。

translations.literal: Ce Ling urgently dispatched orders to send troops at once to cut off Galdan Tseren's line of retreat, but Ma'er Sai would not act on them.
translations.idiomatic: Ce Ling pressed him to march at once and cut off Galdan Tseren's retreat, but Ma'er Sai would not listen.

sentences.zh: 傅鼐進曰：「賊敗亡之餘，可唾手取也！

translations.literal: Fu Nai advanced and said: "The bandits are the remnant of a defeated rout—they can be taken with a turn of the hand!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Nai stepped forward and said, "These are beaten fugitives—you could seize them between your fingers!

sentences.zh: 請發輕騎數千，俾率以戰，事成，功歸大將軍；

translations.literal: Please send out several thousand light cavalry and let me lead them into battle; if the affair succeeds, the merit shall belong to the general-in-chief;
translations.idiomatic: Send me a few thousand light horse and let me lead them. If we win, let the credit go to the commander;

sentences.zh: 事敗，原獨受其罪。

translations.literal: if it fails, I alone will bear the punishment."
translations.idiomatic: if we lose, I alone will answer for it."

sentences.zh: 」馬爾賽默然，再三言不應，至長跪以請，終不許。

translations.literal: Ma'er Sai was silent; again and again Fu Nai spoke and received no assent; he knelt long in entreaty, but in the end was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ma'er Sai said nothing. Fu Nai pleaded again and again; he finally knelt and begged—and was still refused.

sentences.zh: 傅鼐憤甚，將所部出城逐敵。

translations.literal: Fu Nai was furious; he led his own troops out of the city to pursue the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Fu Nai took his own men out of the city in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹策零已遁走，得輜重、牛羊萬計。

translations.literal: Galdan Tseren had already fled; they seized baggage train and livestock by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan Tseren was already gone, but they captured vast stores of baggage and tens of thousands of cattle.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上誅馬爾賽，賚傅鼐花翎。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the Emperor executed Ma'er Sai and bestowed on Fu Nai the peacock plume.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, the Emperor had Ma'er Sai executed and granted Fu Nai the peacock plume.

sentences.zh: 平郡王福彭代為大將軍，傅鼐參贊如故。

translations.literal: Prince Ping of the Commandery, Fu Peng, replaced him as general-in-chief; Fu Nai continued as participating minister as before.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ping Fu Peng replaced Ma'er Sai as commander-in-chief, while Fu Nai kept his post as participating minister.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹策零既大創，不敢深入，師亦未能遠征。

translations.literal: Galdan Tseren, having suffered a great blow, did not dare penetrate deep; the army likewise could not campaign far.
translations.idiomatic: Badly mauled, Galdan Tseren no longer dared push deep inland; the Qing forces, too, could not carry the war far.

sentences.zh: 上召策淩及大將軍查郎阿詣京師廷議，莊親王允祿及策淩等主進討，大學士張廷玉等言不若先撫之，不順則進討。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Ce Ling and the general-in-chief Cha Langa to the capital for a court council; Prince Zhuang Yunlu and Ce Ling and others urged an advance to attack, while Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu and others said it would be better first to pacify them and only advance if they did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor called Ce Ling and Commander-in-Chief Cha Langa to Beijing for a council. Prince Zhuang Yunlu and Ce Ling favored pressing the attack; Zhang Tingyu and other grand secretaries argued for winning them over first and fighting only if they refused.

sentences.zh: 兩議上，上問傅鼐，傅鼐贊撫議。

translations.literal: When both plans were submitted, the Emperor asked Fu Nai; Fu Nai endorsed the pacification plan.
translations.idiomatic: Both views went up; the Emperor asked Fu Nai, and he sided with conciliation.

sentences.zh: 降旨罷兵，遣傅鼐偕內閣學士阿克敦、副都統羅密諭噶爾丹策零。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to cease military operations, and Fu Nai was dispatched together with Grand Secretariat academician Akedun and Vice Commander Luomi to proclaim the message to Galdan Tseren.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered an end to fighting and sent Fu Nai with Grand Secretariat academician Akedun and vice commander Luomi to announce the decision to Galdan Tseren.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹策零欲得阿爾泰山故地，傅鼐力折之。

translations.literal: Galdan Tseren wished to recover the old lands of the Altai Mountains; Fu Nai forcefully overruled him.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan Tseren demanded the old Altai territories; Fu Nai firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 十三年，使還，予都統銜，食俸。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the mission returned, he was granted the rank of commander and given salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, on his return from the embassy, he received commander rank and a salary stipend.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，命署兵部尚書，尋授刑部尚書，仍兼理兵部。

translations.literal: When Gaozong acceded, he was ordered to serve as acting Minister of War; soon he was appointed Minister of Punishments while still concurrently managing War.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianlong took the throne, Fu Nai was made acting minister of war; he was soon appointed minister of punishments while continuing to oversee the war ministry.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，疏言：「刑罰世輕世重。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he memorialized: "Punishments are light in one age and heavy in another.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 (1736) he memorialized: "Punishments grow lighter or heavier from age to age.

sentences.zh: 我朝律例，頒布於順治三年，酌議於康熙十八年，重刊於雍正三年。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's statutes and precedents were promulgated in the third year of Shunzhi, deliberated in the eighteenth year of Kangxi, and reprinted in the third year of Yongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Our code was issued in Shunzhi 3, revised in Kangxi 18, and reprinted in Yongzheng 3.

sentences.zh: 臣伏讀世宗遺詔曰：'凡諸條例，或前本嚴而朕改從寬，此乃昔時部臣定議未協，朕與廷臣悉心斟酌而後更定，應照更定之例行；

translations.literal: Your servant humbly read the testamentary edict of Shizong, which says: 'As to all supplementary regulations, where the earlier text was strict and I changed it to leniency, this was because the ministry officials of old had not agreed in their deliberations; I and the court ministers deliberated with full care and then revised them—those should be carried out according to the revised text;
translations.idiomatic: I have studied Shizong's testamentary edict, which runs: 'Where an earlier regulation was harsh and I softened it, the ministries of old had failed to agree; I and the court ministers weighed it carefully before changing it—follow the revised text;

sentences.zh: 若前本寬而朕改從嚴，此以整飭人心風俗，暫行一時，此後遇事斟酌，若應照舊例者，仍照舊例行。

translations.literal: where the earlier text was lenient and I changed it to severity, this was to rectify human hearts and customs and was to be applied only for a time; hereafter, when matters arise, deliberate—where the old precedent should still apply, still follow the old precedent.'
translations.idiomatic: where an earlier text was lenient and I tightened it, that was to discipline hearts and customs for a season; afterward, weigh each case—where the old rule still fits, keep the old rule.'

sentences.zh: '臣思聖心惓惓於此，蓋必有所軫念而未及更正者也。

translations.literal: 'Your servant reflects that the sage heart was so earnestly concerned with this that there must have been matters he cherished in mind but had not yet corrected.
translations.idiomatic: 'The late Emperor's mind lingered on this point—there must have been provisions he meant to fix but never reached.

sentences.zh: 皇上以世宗之心為心，每遇奏讞，斟酌詳慎。

translations.literal: Your Majesty takes Shizong's heart as his own heart; whenever criminal reports are submitted for decision, he deliberates with full care.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty holds Shizong's intent as his own; on every capital case you deliberate with painstaking care.

sentences.zh: 臣見大清律集解附例一書，現今不行之例猶載其中，恐刑官援引舛錯，吏胥因緣為奸。

translations.literal: Your servant sees that in the book Great Qing Code with Commentary and Attached Precedents, precedents no longer in force are still recorded therein; I fear judicial officers may cite them in error and clerks may use them as openings for fraud.
translations.idiomatic: In the Great Qing Code with Commentary and Attached Precedents, obsolete precedents still appear; judges may cite them wrongly, and clerks will find room for graft.

sentences.zh: 請簡熟悉律例大臣，詳加覈議。

translations.literal: I request that ministers well versed in statutes and precedents be selected to review this in detail.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that skilled jurists be chosen to review the text thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 律文律注，當仍其舊。

translations.literal: The statutory text and statutory commentary should remain as they were.
translations.idiomatic: The articles and their glosses should stand unchanged.

sentences.zh: 所載條例，有今已斟酌改定者，應從改定；

translations.literal: Among the precedents recorded, those already deliberated and revised should follow the revision;
translations.idiomatic: Among the listed precedents, those already revised should follow the revision;

sentences.zh: 有應斟酌而未逮者，悉照舊章：務歸於平允，逐條繕摺，恭請欽定纂輯頒布。

translations.literal: those that ought to be deliberated but have not yet been reached should all follow the old regulations: strive to return to evenhandedness, copy out each item in a memorial, and respectfully request imperial approval for compilation and promulgation.
translations.idiomatic: those still awaiting deliberation should keep the old rule until weighed—aim for even justice, set out each item in a memorial, and seek Your Majesty's approval to compile and promulgate a corrected edition.

sentences.zh: 」得旨允行。

translations.literal: " The instruction was received and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「斷獄引用律例，宜審全文。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "In adjudicating cases one should cite statutes and precedents only after reading the full text.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "In sentencing, one must read a statute or precedent whole.

sentences.zh: 若摘引律語，入人重罪，是為深文週內。

translations.literal: If one extracts phrases from the statute to impose heavy guilt on a person, that is to twist the law and ensnare him within it.
translations.idiomatic: To pluck a phrase from the code and hang a heavy crime on someone is to twist the law into a trap.

sentences.zh: 律載：'官吏懷挾私仇，故勘平人致死者，斬監候。

translations.literal: The code provides: 'If an official, harboring a private grudge, deliberately investigates an innocent commoner and causes his death, decapitation with suspension.
translations.idiomatic: The code says: 'An official who, nursing private hatred, deliberately frames an innocent commoner and causes his death, is sentenced to decapitation, execution suspended.

sentences.zh: '又載：'若因公事干連在官，事須問鞫，依法拷訊，邂逅致死者，勿論。

translations.literal: ' It also provides: 'If, because of a public matter, a person under official investigation must be questioned, and under lawful torture he dies by mischance, no penalty.
translations.idiomatic: ' It also says: 'If, in the course of official business, a person held for questioning dies under lawful torture by accident, no penalty applies.

sentences.zh: '律意本極平允。

translations.literal: ' The intent of the code is in itself thoroughly evenhanded.
translations.idiomatic: ' The statute's intent is perfectly evenhanded.

sentences.zh: 數年來，各督撫遇屬員誤將在官人犯拷訊致死，輒摘引'故勘平人'一語，擬斬監候。

translations.literal: In recent years, whenever governors-general and governors encountered subordinates who by mistake tortured to death a person under official investigation, they would extract the phrase 'deliberately investigates an innocent commoner' and propose decapitation with suspension.
translations.idiomatic: For years, whenever a governor-general or governor found a subordinate who had tortured a detainee to death by mistake, he would quote 'deliberately investigates an innocent commoner' and recommend suspended decapitation.

sentences.zh: 尚書張照又奏准：'如將笞杖人犯故意夾拷致死二命以上，及徒流人犯四命以上，俱以故勘平人論。

translations.literal: Minister Zhang Zhao also memorialized for approval: 'If one deliberately uses the leg-press to torture to death two or more persons liable to beating with the bamboo, or four or more persons liable to penal servitude or exile, all are to be judged as deliberately investigating an innocent commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Zhao had also won approval for a rule: 'If an officer deliberately racks to death two or more persons liable only to bamboo strokes, or four or more liable to penal servitude or exile, treat the case as deliberate framing of an innocent.

sentences.zh: '不思既非懷挾私仇，於故勘之義何居？

translations.literal: ' Yet if there was no harboring of private grudge, how does that fit the meaning of deliberate investigation?
translations.idiomatic: ' Yet where is the private grudge that 'deliberate framing' requires?

sentences.zh: 若謂在官之人本屬無罪，則必有誣告之人，應照律抵罪；

translations.literal: If one says that a person under official investigation was originally without guilt, then there must have been a false accuser, who should be punished according to the code;
translations.idiomatic: If the detainee was truly innocent, there must have been a false accuser to punish under the code;

sentences.zh: 若​​謂輕罪不應夾訊，命盜等案，當首從未分，安能預定為笞杖為徒流？

translations.literal: if one says that a light offense should not be tortured with the leg-press, in cases of robbery with violence the principal and accessories are not yet distinguished—how can one predetermine in advance whether they are liable to bamboo or to penal servitude or exile?
translations.idiomatic: if one says light crimes should not be racked, in robbery and banditry cases principal and accessory are not yet sorted—how can one know in advance whether the penalty will be bamboo, servitude, or exile?

sentences.zh: 若謂拷訊不依法，自有'決罰不如法'律在，致死二人、四人以上，當議以加等。

translations.literal: If one says the torture was not according to law, there is already the statute 'punishment not according to law'; when two persons or four or more are killed, one should deliberate increased penalties.
translations.idiomatic: If the torture was unlawful, the statute on 'punishment not according to law' already applies; when two or four or more die, increase the penalty by due degrees.

sentences.zh: 請敕法司酌改平允。

translations.literal: I request that the Ministry of Punishments be ordered to deliberate and revise to evenhandedness.
translations.idiomatic: I ask the Ministry of Punishments to revise the rule to something fair.

sentences.zh: 」下部議行。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was referred to the ministries for action.

sentences.zh: 是秋，以勒借商銀，回奏不實，奪官。

translations.literal: That autumn, for compelling merchants to lend silver and for an untruthful memorial in reply, his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he lost his rank for forcing merchants to lend silver and for lying about it in his report.

sentences.zh: 尋命暫署兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to serve temporarily as acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting minister of war again.

sentences.zh: 二年，授正藍旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Commander of the Plain Blue Banner Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was named commander of the Plain Blue Manchu Banner.

sentences.zh: 三年，坐違例發俸，發往軍台效力。

translations.literal: In the third year, for disbursing salaries in violation of regulations, he was sent to labor at military courier stations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was punished for paying salaries contrary to rule and sent to serve at military courier stations.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
