translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 陳儀，字子翽，順天文安人。

translations.literal: Chen Yi, courtesy name Zishuo, was a native of Wen'an in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi, styled Zishuo, came from Wen'an in the Shuntian metropolitan district.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十四年進士，改庶吉士，散館授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year of Kangxi he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and after leaving the Academy was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Kangxi 54, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and on leaving the Academy became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 為古文辭，治經世學，大學士硃軾器之。

translations.literal: He wrote in the ancient literary style and studied statecraft; Grand Secretary Zhu Shi valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote classical prose and studied practical statecraft; Grand Secretary Zhu Shi took him seriously.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，直隸大水，諸河氾濫，壞田廬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng, Zhili suffered great floods; the rivers overflowed and ruined fields and houses.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 3, Zhili was swept by flood; rivers burst their banks and wrecked fields and homes.

sentences.zh: 世宗命怡親王允祥偕軾相度濬治。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Prince Yi Yinxiang together with Zhu Shi to survey and dredge for treatment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Prince Yi Yinxiang with Zhu Shi to survey the rivers and plan dredging.

sentences.zh: 王求諳習畿輔水利者，軾以儀對。

translations.literal: The Prince sought someone versed in water conservancy in the capital region; Zhu Shi named Chen Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked for an expert on metropolitan waterworks; Zhu Shi recommended Chen Yi.

sentences.zh: 延見，諮治河所宜先，儀曰：「硃子言治河先低處。

translations.literal: Summoned for an audience, he was asked what should be done first in governing the rivers; Chen Yi said: "Zhu Xi said that in governing rivers one should begin with the low places.
translations.idiomatic: Called in for audience, he was asked where river work should start. Chen Yi answered: "Zhu Xi taught that one must begin with the lowest ground.

sentences.zh: 天津為古渤海逆河之會，百川之尾閭。

translations.literal: Tianjin is where the ancient Bohai's counter-flowing rivers met, the final estuary of a hundred streams.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin is where the old Bohai tides met the land—the tail of a hundred rivers.

sentences.zh: 今南北二運河、東西兩淀盛漲，爭趨三岔口，而強潮復來拒之，牴牾洄漩而不時下，下隘則上溢，其勢宜然。

translations.literal: Today the north and south Grand Canals and the eastern and western marshes swell together and rush toward Sankou; yet the strong tide comes back to block them, colliding and swirling without timely discharge—when the outlet is narrow, the upper reaches must overflow; the tendency is inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: Now the northern and southern Grand Canals and the eastern and western lakes all rise together and pour toward Sankou, while the sea tide pushes back. Water collides, eddies, and cannot drain; when the mouth is narrow, the upper reaches must flood—that is only natural.

sentences.zh: 故欲治河，莫如先擴達海之口。

translations.literal: Therefore, to govern the rivers, nothing is better than first widening the mouth where they reach the sea.
translations.idiomatic: To govern the rivers, then, one must first widen the sea mouth.

sentences.zh: 欲擴海口，莫如先減入口之水。

translations.literal: To widen the sea mouth, nothing is better than first reducing the water entering at the head.
translations.idiomatic: To widen the sea mouth, one must first cut the water entering upstream.

sentences.zh: 入口之水減，則達海之口寬。

translations.literal: When the water at the entrance is reduced, the mouth reaching the sea becomes wide.
translations.idiomatic: Less water at the head means a wider passage to the sea.

sentences.zh: 北永定，南子牙，中七十二沽，皆得沛然入三岔口而東注矣。

translations.literal: Northward the Yongding, southward the Ziya, and between them the seventy-two gu of the metropolitan region could all pour freely into Sankou and flow east.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Yongding in the north, the Ziya in the south, and the seventy-two gu between them could all rush freely through Sankou to the east.

sentences.zh: 」四年春，從王行視水利，教令章奏皆出儀手。

translations.literal: " In the spring of the fourth year he followed the Prince on an inspection of waterworks; all instructions and memorials were drafted by Chen Yi.
translations.idiomatic: " In the spring of the fourth year he toured the works with the prince; every instruction and memorial came from Chen Yi's hand.

sentences.zh: 軾以憂歸，王薦於朝，命以侍講署天津同知。

translations.literal: When Zhu Shi returned home in mourning, the Prince recommended him to the court; he was ordered to serve as acting subprefect of Tianjin while holding the post of lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Shi went home on mourning leave, the prince recommended him; the court named him acting Tianjin subprefect while he kept his lectureship.

sentences.zh: 轉侍讀，擢庶子，仍署同知如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to reader, promoted to tutor, and still served as acting subprefect as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to reader, then tutor, and still held the Tianjin post.

sentences.zh: 五年，王奏設水利營田四局，儀領天津局，兼督文安、大城堤工。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Prince memorialized to establish four bureaus for water conservancy and military colony farming; Chen Yi headed the Tianjin bureau and also supervised dike works in Wen'an and Dacheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the prince proposed four bureaus for waterworks and military colony farming; Chen Yi ran the Tianjin bureau and oversaw dikes in Wen'an and Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 二縣地卑下，積潦不消。

translations.literal: The land of the two counties was low-lying; standing water would not drain away.
translations.idiomatic: Both counties lie low; floodwater would not drain.

sentences.zh: 是秋復大水，堤內外皆巨浸。

translations.literal: That autumn floods came again; inside and outside the dikes were vast inundations.
translations.idiomatic: Floods returned that autumn; water stood on both sides of the dikes.

sentences.zh: 儀購秫稭十餘萬束，立表下楗以御水。

translations.literal: Chen Yi purchased more than a hundred thousand bundles of sorghum stalks and set up gauge posts with piles driven below to hold back the water.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi bought more than a hundred thousand bundles of sorghum stalks and drove piles with gauge marks to hold the flood.

sentences.zh: 堤本民工，儀言於王，請發帑興修，招民就工代賑，堤得完固。

translations.literal: Dike labor had been corvée of the people; Chen Yi spoke to the Prince and requested treasury funds for construction, hiring the people for work in place of relief grain—thus the dikes were completed and made solid.
translations.idiomatic: Dike work had relied on corvée; Chen Yi persuaded the prince to fund repairs from the treasury and hire laborers with relief grain—so the dikes were finished and held.

sentences.zh: 南運河長屯堤地隸靜海，吏舞法，歲調發霸州、文安、大城民協修，百里裹糧，咸以為苦，儀為除其籍。

translations.literal: The Changtun dike lands on the Southern Grand Canal fell under Jinghai; officials twisted the law, and each year they conscripted people from Bazhou, Wen'an, and Dacheng to help repair—a hundred li from home, carrying their own grain, all regarded it as hardship; Chen Yi had them removed from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The Changtun dike on the Southern Canal lay in Jinghai; corrupt clerks each year drafted men from Bazhou, Wen'an, and Dacheng to help repair a hundred li from home at their own expense. Chen Yi struck their names from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 畿輔大小諸河七十餘，疏故濬新，儀所勘定殆十六七雲。

translations.literal: Of more than seventy great and small rivers in the capital region, in dredging the old and opening the new, those Chen Yi surveyed and fixed amounted to roughly sixteen or seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: Of more than seventy rivers large and small in the capital region, he surveyed and settled perhaps sixteen or seventeen, dredging old channels and cutting new ones.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to lecturer in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to Hanlin lecturer.

sentences.zh: 時議設營田觀察使二員，分轄京東西，以督率州縣。

translations.literal: At the time it was proposed to establish two surveillance commissioners for military colony farming, each overseeing the eastern and western parts of the capital region to supervise the prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: The court then debated two surveillance commissioners for military colony farming, one for each side of the capital region, to drive the prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 命儀以僉都御史充京東營田觀察使，營田於天津。

translations.literal: Chen Yi was ordered to serve as surveillance commissioner for military colony farming in the eastern capital region, with rank as vice censor-in-chief, and to open colonies at Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi was named eastern commissioner with vice censor-in-chief rank and opened colonies at Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 仿明汪應蛟遺制，築十字圍，三面開渠，與海河通。

translations.literal: Following the legacy system of Wang Yingjiao of the Ming, he built cross-shaped enclosures; on three sides he opened canals communicating with the Hai River.
translations.idiomatic: Following Ming Wang Yingjiao's method, he built cross-shaped polders and cut canals on three sides into the Hai River.

sentences.zh: 潮來渠滿，閉渠蓄水以供灌溉，白塘、葛沽間斥鹵盡變膏腴。

translations.literal: When the tide came the canals filled; closing the canals stored water for irrigation, and between Baitang and Gegu the salt flats all turned to rich soil.
translations.idiomatic: When the tide rose the canals filled; closing them stored irrigation water, and the salt flats between Baitang and Gegu turned to fertile fields.

sentences.zh: 豐潤、玉田地多沮洳，儀教之開渠築圩，皆成良田。

translations.literal: In Fengrun and Yutian much land was waterlogged marsh; Chen Yi taught them to open canals and build embankments, and all became good fields.
translations.idiomatic: In Fengrun and Yutian much land was bog; he taught them to dig canals and build dikes until the ground became good farmland.

sentences.zh: 十一年，大雨，山水暴發，沒田廬。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year great rains fell; mountain torrents burst forth and submerged fields and houses.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year heavy rains sent mountain floods over fields and homes.

sentences.zh: 儀疏聞，諭籌賑，即命儀董其事，凡賑三十四萬餘口。

translations.literal: Chen Yi memorialized to report; he was instructed to plan relief, and at once was ordered to take charge of the matter; in all more than three hundred forty thousand persons were relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi reported the disaster; ordered to organize relief, he took charge at once and fed more than three hundred forty thousand people.

sentences.zh: 十二年，轉侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to reader in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he became Hanlin reader.

sentences.zh: 尋罷觀察使，還京師。

translations.literal: Before long the surveillance commissionership was abolished and he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the commissionership was abolished and he returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 儀篤於內行，先世遺田數百畝，悉推以讓兄。

translations.literal: Chen Yi was devoted in his conduct within the family; several hundred mu of fields left by his forebears he wholly yielded to his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi was scrupulous in family duty; he gave his elder brother every mu of the few hundred his ancestors had left.

sentences.zh: 既仕，分祿畀昆弟，週諸故舊。

translations.literal: After he took office, he divided his salary among his brothers and supported old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he shared his salary with his brothers and helped old friends.

sentences.zh: 有故人子貧甚，囑門生為謀生業，事為人所訐，吏議當降調。

translations.literal: There was the son of an old friend who was extremely poor; he entrusted a student to find him a livelihood; the matter was denounced by someone, and the officials deliberated that he should be demoted.
translations.idiomatic: A friend's son was desperately poor; he asked a student to find him work. Someone reported the favor, and the personnel office recommended demotion.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，授鴻臚寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong he was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2 he was made vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 儀以老乞歸。

translations.literal: Chen Yi begged to retire on grounds of age.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on grounds of age.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 子玉友，雍正八年進士，官台灣知府。

translations.literal: His son Yuyou, a metropolitan graduate in the eighth year of Yongzheng, served as prefect of Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuyou, a metropolitan graduate of Yongzheng 8, became prefect of Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 勤其官，有惠政。

translations.literal: He was diligent in his office and had policies that brought benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He served diligently and left a record of kindness.

sentences.zh: 劉師恕，字艾堂，江南寶應人。

translations.literal: Liu Shishu, courtesy name Aitang, was a native of Baoying in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shishu, styled Aitang, came from Baoying in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父國黻，康熙二十一年進士，改庶吉士，授戶科給事中，歷督捕理事官。

translations.literal: His father Guofu, a metropolitan graduate in the twenty-first year of Kangxi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and served in turn as commissioner for bandit suppression.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guofu, a metropolitan graduate of Kangxi 21, entered the Hanlin, became a revenue supervising secretary, and later commissioner for bandit suppression.

sentences.zh: 在戶科，建言民田畝有大小，地有上中下，請具載簡明賦役全書，明示天下。

translations.literal: While in the Ministry of Revenue, he memorialized that commoners' fields had large and small mu and land of upper, middle, and lower grades; he asked that these be fully recorded in the concise Complete Book of Taxes and Corvée and made plain to the empire.
translations.idiomatic: At Revenue he argued that peasant fields differed in mu size and in upper, middle, and lower grade; he asked that the concise Complete Book of Taxes and Corvée record all of this plainly for the empire.

sentences.zh: 在督捕，詳考則例刊布之。

translations.literal: While commissioner for bandit suppression, he examined the regulations in detail and had them published.
translations.idiomatic: As bandit-suppression commissioner he studied the regulations in detail and had them printed.

sentences.zh: 往時以逃人為根，以一累百十，以逃案為市。

translations.literal: Formerly, because fugitives were made the root of a case, one man might implicate a hundred or ten; fugitive cases became a trade.
translations.idiomatic: Once, a single fugitive could drag down scores of innocents; fugitive cases had become a racket.

sentences.zh: 取所歷州縣官職名待劾，弊不勝詰，皆剔除之，乃裁併兵部。

translations.literal: He took the names and offices of officials he had served under in various prefectures and counties and held them pending impeachment; the abuses could not withstand inquiry, and all were eliminated; then the Ministry of War was reduced in size.
translations.idiomatic: He listed every magistrate he had known for impeachment; the abuses could not survive scrutiny and were struck out, and the Ministry of War was cut down.

sentences.zh: 改授鴻臚寺卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 師恕，三十九年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: Shishu, a metropolitan graduate in the thirty-ninth year, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: Shishu passed the metropolitan examination in the thirty-ninth year, entered the Hanlin, and became a proofreader.

sentences.zh: 累遷國子監祭酒。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，授貴州布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was appointed Governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he was made governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷通政使，轉左副都御史，擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Commissioner of the Office of Transmission, then to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, and promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became transmission commissioner, then left vice censor-in-chief, then vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 上以宜兆熊署直隸總督，調師恕禮部，協理總督事。

translations.literal: Because Yi Zhaoxiong was acting Governor-General of Zhili, Shishu was transferred to the Ministry of Rites to assist in managing the governor-general's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi Zhaoxiong was acting governor-general of Zhili, Shishu was moved to Rites to help run the province.

sentences.zh: 五年，奏獲交河妖民孫守禮，嚴鞫治罪。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he memorialized the capture of the sorcerer Sun Shouli of Jiaohe and had him strictly interrogated and punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he reported the arrest of the Jiaohe sorcerer Sun Shouli, had him tortured, and punished him.

sentences.zh: 上獎其遇事直達，不稍隱諱。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised him for reporting matters directly without the least concealment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his habit of reporting straight, without concealment.

sentences.zh: 師恕與兆熊議裁學政陋規，學政孫嘉淦言：「學政舊規，日得五十五兩，今減半即足用。

translations.literal: Shishu and Yi Zhaoxiong deliberated cutting the shabby customary fees of the educational commissioner; Educational Commissioner Sun Jiagan said: "The old custom for the educational commissioner was fifty-five taels a day; halving it would be enough.
translations.idiomatic: Shishu and Yi Zhaoxiong debated abolishing the educational commissioner's customary fees. Commissioner Sun Jiagan said: "The old allowance was fifty-five taels a day; half would suffice.

sentences.zh: 」師恕言：「減至一兩亦不可行，當另奏撥解公費。

translations.literal: " Shishu said: "Even reducing it to one tael would not be workable; public funds should be allocated by a separate memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " Shishu replied: "Cutting it to one tael would still not work; public funds must be supplied by separate appropriation.

sentences.zh: 」師恕與兆熊奏已與嘉淦會商裁革，嘉淦以實奏。

translations.literal: " Shishu and Yi Zhaoxiong memorialized that they had already consulted with Jiagan and cut the fees; Jiagan reported the facts.
translations.idiomatic: " They memorialized that they had already consulted Jiagan and cut the fees; Jiagan told the truth in his own report.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「孫嘉淦非騷擾貪饕者比，爾等何不量至此？

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed: "Sun Jiagan is not to be compared with those who harass and gorge themselves; why did you not measure matters to this point?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked them: "Sun Jiagan is no harassing glutton—how could you push him this far?

sentences.zh: 可仍循舊例而行。

translations.literal: You may still follow the old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Let the old custom stand.

sentences.zh: 嘉淦，端士也，宜作成之。

translations.literal: Jiagan is an upright gentleman; you should help him grow into his role.
translations.idiomatic: Jiagan is an upright man; cultivate him.

sentences.zh: 」初夏，保定諸府少雨，上以為憂。

translations.literal: " In early summer the prefectures around Baoding had little rain; the Emperor was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: " Early that summer Baoding and neighboring prefectures saw little rain, and the Emperor grew anxious.

sentences.zh: 師恕等言：「今歲遇閏，此後得雨不遲。

translations.literal: Shishu and others said: "This year has an intercalary month; rain will not be late thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Shishu and his colleagues said: "This is a leap year; rain will come in good time.

sentences.zh: 」上責其怠忽。

translations.literal: " The Emperor rebuked them for negligence.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor scolded them for complacency.

sentences.zh: 尋奏裁驛站夫馬工料羨餘銀，上諭曰：「陋規自應裁，第當量情酌理為之，毋過刻，令後來地方諸事難於措辦也。

translations.literal: Soon they memorialized cutting the surplus silver from courier stations' labor, fodder, and supplies; the Emperor instructed: "Shabby customs should indeed be cut, but you must weigh circumstances and reason in doing so; do not be too harsh and make it hard for those who come after to manage local affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They soon memorialized to cut surplus funds for courier stations, horses, and supplies. The Emperor wrote: "Abuses should be cut, but weigh each case—do not be so harsh that later officials cannot govern.

sentences.zh: 」調吏部，仍留協理。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel while still retained to assist in management.
translations.idiomatic: " He was moved to Personnel but kept on as co-administrator.

sentences.zh: 大名諸生竇相可訴知府曾逢聖貪劣，布政使張適杖殺之，以獄斃報，兆熊、師恕匿不以聞。

translations.literal: Dou Xiangke, a licentiate of Daming, accused Prefect Zeng Fengsheng of greed and misconduct; Financial Commissioner Zhang Shi beat him to death and reported that he had died in prison; Yi Zhaoxiong and Shishu concealed the matter and did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Xiangke, a Daming licentiate, accused Prefect Zeng Fengsheng of corruption; Financial Commissioner Zhang Shi beat him to death and reported a prison death. Yi Zhaoxiong and Shishu hid the truth.

sentences.zh: 上命尚書福敏等按治得實，兆熊坐降調，上寬師恕，諭責其徇隱，命何世璂署直隸總督，仍令師恕協理。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Minister Fu Min and others to investigate; the facts were established; Yi Zhaoxiong was demoted, while the Emperor was lenient toward Shishu, instructing and rebuking him for concealment, ordered He Shiji to act as Governor-General of Zhili, and still had Shishu assist in management.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Minister Fu Min to investigate; the facts stood. Yi Zhaoxiong was demoted; Shishu was spared but rebuked for concealment. He Shiji was named acting governor-general of Zhili, with Shishu still assisting.

sentences.zh: 七年，命師恕以內閣學士充福建觀風整俗使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Shishu was ordered to serve as Grand Secretariat academician and Commissioner for Surveying Customs and Reforming Morals in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was named Grand Secretariat academician and Fujian commissioner for surveying customs and reforming morals.

sentences.zh: 八年，疏言：「海澄公舊以轄兵給印，後兵裁而印未繳。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he memorialized: "The Lord of Haicheng formerly had his command troops issued seals; later the troops were cut but the seal was not surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he memorialized: "The Lord of Haicheng once had his command troops issued official seals; when the troops were later reduced, the seal was never returned.

sentences.zh: 今海澄公黃應纘濫行印文，非所宜，當令繳銷。

translations.literal: Now Huang Yingxuan, Lord of Haicheng, abuses the seal in issuing documents—this is not fitting; he should be ordered to surrender it for cancellation.
translations.idiomatic: Now Huang Yingxuan of Haicheng abuses that seal in official documents. That should not be allowed; he must be ordered to surrender it for cancellation.

sentences.zh: 」並言外省世襲武職，年及二十，當令諮部引見，分京外學習。

translations.literal: " He also said that hereditary military posts in the provinces, when the holder reaches twenty, should be ordered to consult the ministry and be presented at court, to study in the capital or in the provinces respectively.
translations.idiomatic: " He also urged that provincial holders of hereditary military posts, once they reached twenty, be sent to the ministry for presentation at court and assigned to study either in the capital or in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 部議從之。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 十一年，師恕以病告，省觀風整俗使不復設。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Shishu reported illness; the Commissioner for Observing Customs and Reforming Morals was not re-established.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Shishu took leave for illness, and the post of Commissioner for Observing Customs and Reforming Morals was not filled again.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年，寶應災，治賑，非貧民例不給。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong, when Baoying suffered disaster, he managed relief; except by rule for the poor, none were given.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 7, when Baoying was stricken by disaster, he directed relief—but by rule only the truly poor received aid.

sentences.zh: 師恕族人諸生洞嗾不得賑者，閧堂罷市。

translations.literal: Shishu's clansmen, licentiates who had stirred up those not receiving relief, stormed the yamen and shut the markets.
translations.idiomatic: Licentiates among Shishu's kin had incited those denied relief; they stormed his yamen and shut down the markets.

sentences.zh: 上責師恕不能約束，奪官。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked Shishu for inability to restrain them and stripped his office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor blamed Shishu for failing to keep order and stripped him of rank.

sentences.zh: 南巡迎謁，賜侍讀學士銜。

translations.literal: When the Emperor toured the south, Shishu came out to welcome him and was granted the title of Reader of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern tour Shishu came forward to welcome the throne and was given the title Reader of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-first year.

sentences.zh: 是時廣東、湖南皆置觀風整俗使。

translations.literal: At that time both Guangdong and Hunan had Commissioners for Observing Customs and Reforming Morals.
translations.idiomatic: By then Guangdong and Hunan each had a Commissioner for Observing Customs and Reforming Morals.

sentences.zh: 焦祈年，字穀貽，山東章丘人。

translations.literal: Jiao Qinian, courtesy name Guyi, was a native of Zhangqiu in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Qinian, styled Guyi, came from Zhangqiu in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he passed the metropolitan examination as a jinshi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Yongzheng 1, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 考選雲南道御史，擢順天府丞，權府尹，遷右通政。

translations.literal: Selected by examination as a censor of the Yunnan circuit, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Shuntian Prefecture, acted as prefect, and was transferred to Right Vice Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen censor for the Yunnan circuit, he rose to vice director of Shuntian prefecture, served as acting prefect, then became right vice commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 八年，命充廣東觀風整俗使，修建十府、二州書院，延通人為之師。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to serve as Guangdong Commissioner for Observing Customs and Reforming Morals; he built academies in ten prefectures and two subprefectures and invited learned men to serve as teachers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made Guangdong Commissioner for Observing Customs and Reforming Morals. He founded academies in ten prefectures and two subprefectures and brought in scholars to teach.

sentences.zh: 濱海多盜，設策鉤捕，得劇盜百餘置諸法，盜差熄。

translations.literal: Along the coast bandits were numerous; he set stratagems to lure and seize them, got more than a hundred notorious bandits and punished them by law, and banditry largely ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The coast swarmed with pirates; he laid traps, captured more than a hundred notorious offenders, and punished them under law until piracy largely died away.

sentences.zh: 奸民以符劄惑眾，擒治之，赦其株連者。

translations.literal: Wicked men used talisman slips to delude the masses; he seized and punished them and pardoned those implicated by association.
translations.idiomatic: Rascals were deceiving crowds with talisman slips; he arrested and punished the ringleaders and pardoned those caught only by association.

sentences.zh: 西洋人置天主堂，使徙歸澳門。

translations.literal: Westerners had set up Catholic churches; he made them move back to Macao.
translations.idiomatic: Westerners had built Catholic churches; he ordered them back to Macao.

sentences.zh: 簡閱營伍，軍政以肅。

translations.literal: He inspected the garrisons and troops; military administration was thereby made strict.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the garrisons and tightened military discipline.

sentences.zh: 擢光祿寺卿，召為順天府尹，旋調奉天。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, summoned to be Prefect of Shuntian, and soon transferred to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, he was recalled to serve as Shuntian prefect and soon moved to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 行次山海關，疾作，乞歸，卒於裡。

translations.literal: En route, at Shanhaiguan, illness seized him; he begged to return home and died in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: On the road, at Shanhaiguan, he fell ill, asked to go home, and died there.

sentences.zh: 李徽，字元綸，山西崞縣人。

translations.literal: Li Hui, courtesy name Yuanlun, was a native of Guo County in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui, styled Yuanlun, came from Guo County in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年，鄉試舉第一。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year of Kangxi he placed first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 52 he ranked first in the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年進士，改庶吉士，散館刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he passed as jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and on leaving the academy was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Yongzheng 1, entered the Hanlin, and on leaving the academy became a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 尋复授檢討。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed a compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was reappointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 考選浙江道御史。

translations.literal: Selected by examination as a censor of the Zhejiang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen censor for the Zhejiang circuit.

sentences.zh: 是時遣御史巡察順天直隸諸府，順天、永平、宣化為一員，保定、正定、河間為一員，順德、廣平、大名為一員，徽巡察順德、廣平、大名三府。

translations.literal: At that time censors were dispatched to inspect the prefectures of Shuntian and Zhili: Shuntian, Yongping, and Xuanhua were one inspector; Baoding, Zhengding, and Hejian another; Shunde, Guangping, and Daming a third. Hui inspected the three prefectures of Shunde, Guangping, and Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Censors were then touring Shuntian and the Zhili prefectures in groups of three—Shuntian, Yongping, and Xuanhua; Baoding, Zhengding, and Hejian; Shunde, Guangping, and Daming. Hui was assigned the last group.

sentences.zh: 曾靜、張熙事起，上慮湖南士民為所惑，議遣使循行訓迪。

translations.literal: When the affair of Zeng Jing and Zhang Xi arose, the Emperor feared the gentry and people of Hunan might be misled by them and discussed sending an envoy to travel the circuit instructing and guiding them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zeng Jing and Zhang Xi case broke, the Emperor worried that Hunan's scholars and commoners might be swayed and considered sending someone to tour the province with guidance.

sentences.zh: 以大學士硃軾薦，遣徽勸諭化導。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Grand Secretary Zhu Shi, Hui was dispatched to exhort, persuade, and transform them.
translations.idiomatic: On Grand Secretary Zhu Shi's recommendation, Hui was sent to exhort and guide the people.

sentences.zh: 尋授僉都御史，充湖南觀風整俗使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and made Hunan Commissioner for Observing Customs and Reforming Morals.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice censor-in-chief and Hunan Commissioner for Observing Customs and Reforming Morals.

sentences.zh: 徽在官四年，察吏安民，能稱其職。

translations.literal: Hui served four years in office, examining officials and settling the people, and could be said to fill his post.
translations.idiomatic: For four years he examined officials and steadied the people and acquitted himself well.

sentences.zh: 坐事，降授倉監督。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted and appointed Superintendent of the Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: After an offense he was demoted to superintendent of the granaries.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，命复官，遽卒。

translations.literal: When Gaozong acceded, he was ordered to restore his office, but soon died.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianlong took the throne his rank was restored, but he died almost at once.

sentences.zh: 廣西學政衛昌績請設觀風整俗使，御史陳宏謀繼請。

translations.literal: Guangxi Educational Commissioner Wei Changji requested establishment of a Commissioner for Observing Customs and Reforming Morals; Censor Chen Hongmou again requested it.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi educational commissioner Wei Changji asked for such a commissioner; Censor Chen Hongmou pressed the request again.

sentences.zh: 上諭宏謀等曰：「廣西通籍者本少，乃已有狂悖如謝濟世、陸生柟者，風俗薄劣可見。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed Hongmou and the others: "Guangxi has always had few men registered at court, yet there are already such reckless men as Xie Jishi and Lu Shengnan—how inferior the customs may be seen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Hongmou and his colleagues: "Guangxi has always sent few men to the capital, yet you already have reckless figures like Xie Jishi and Lu Shengnan—its morals speak for themselves.

sentences.zh: 爾等不能端本澂源，躬先表率，而望秉鐸司教之官，家喻戶曉，易俗移風，所謂逐末而忘其本也。

translations.literal: You cannot rectify the root and clarify the source, set the example yourselves in person, yet expect officials who hold the scepter and teach to make every household understand, change customs and shift the wind—that is what is called chasing the branch and forgetting the root.
translations.idiomatic: You cannot set the root right and lead by example yourselves, yet expect every magistrate who holds the staff of office to preach in every household and shift the wind of custom—that is to chase the branch and forget the root.

sentences.zh: 」議寢未行。

translations.literal: " The proposal was shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 王國棟，字左吾，漢軍鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Wang Guodong, courtesy name Zuowu, was a Chinese Bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guodong, styled Zuowu, was a Hanjun of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年進士，改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year of Kangxi he passed as jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Kangxi 52, entered the Hanlin, and became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，查嗣庭、汪景祺坐文字謗訕見法。

translations.literal: In the early Yongzheng period, Cha Siting and Wang Jingqi were punished by law for writings that slandered.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng's reign Cha Siting and Wang Jingqi were executed for seditious writings.

sentences.zh: 上謂浙江士習澆漓，四年，設浙江觀風整俗使，以授國棟。

translations.literal: The Emperor said the scholarly habits of Zhejiang were corrupt; in the fourth year he established the Zhejiang Commissioner for Observing Customs and Reforming Morals and gave it to Guodong.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged Zhejiang scholarship corrupt. In the fourth year he created the Zhejiang commissioner post and gave it to Guodong.

sentences.zh: 國棟至官，巡行宣諭，清逋賦，懲唆訟，飭營伍，嚴保甲，次第疏聞，上溫諭獎之。

translations.literal: When Guodong reached his post he toured proclaiming the imperial will, cleared arrears in tax, punished those who stirred up litigation, disciplined the garrisons, tightened the baojia system, and reported each matter in turn by memorial; the Emperor warmly praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching office he toured the province proclaiming the throne's will, cleared tax arrears, punished litigation brokers, drilled the troops, tightened the baojia system, and reported each step by memorial. The Emperor praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 遷宗人府府丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 五年，上以浙江被水，米貴，命國棟同巡撫李衛發庫帑四萬，於杭州、嘉興、湖州三府修城、濬河、築堤，俾饑民就傭食力。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, because Zhejiang had suffered flooding and rice was dear, the Emperor ordered Guodong together with Governor Li Wei to disburse forty thousand taels from the treasury at Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou to repair city walls, dredge rivers, and build dikes, so that famine victims might find work for food and wages.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year floods had driven up rice prices in Zhejiang. The Emperor ordered Guodong and Governor Li Wei to release forty thousand taels from the treasury for repairs at Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou—city walls, river dredging, dikes—so hungry men could earn their food by labor.

sentences.zh: 國棟奏：「杭州至海寧塘河淤，當濬治。

translations.literal: Guodong memorialized: "From Hangzhou to the Haichang seawall the canal is silted and should be dredged.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong reported: "The canal from Hangzhou to the Haichang seawall is choked with silt and must be dredged.

sentences.zh: 太湖堤閘及嘉興石塘多傾圮，當修理。

translations.literal: The dikes, sluices, and stone works of Lake Tai and Jiaxing are largely collapsed and should be repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Lake Tai's dikes and sluices and Jiaxing's stone seawalls have largely collapsed and need repair.

sentences.zh: 冬春雨雪，工作多費，請俟九、十月水落興工。

translations.literal: In winter and spring rain and snow make the work costly; please wait until the ninth and tenth months when the water falls to begin construction."
translations.idiomatic: Winter and spring rains will drive up costs; please wait until the ninth and tenth months, when the water drops, to start work."

sentences.zh: 」上韙之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尋擢湖南巡撫，以許容代為浙江觀風整俗使。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Governor of Hunan; Xu Rong replaced him as Zhejiang Commissioner for Observing Customs and Reforming Morals.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Hunan governor; Xu Rong replaced him as Zhejiang commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上諭國棟曰：「初欲令爾在浙整飭數年，俾收成效。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed Guodong: "At first I wished to keep you in Zhejiang several years to reform matters and gather real results.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Guodong: "I had meant to keep you in Zhejiang several years until the work showed real fruit.

sentences.zh: 但湖南廢弛久，今以命爾，爾其勉之！

translations.literal: But Hunan has long been neglected; now I give you this charge—do your utmost!"
translations.idiomatic: But Hunan has been neglected too long; I give you that province instead—do your utmost!"

sentences.zh: 」上命湖廣總督邁柱修兩省堤工。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Huguang Governor-General Mai Zhu to repair the dikes of both provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Huguang governor-general Mai Zhu to repair dikes in both provinces.

sentences.zh: 國棟疏言：「湘陰、巴陵、華容、安鄉、澧、武陵、龍陽、沅江、益陽九州縣環繞洞庭，居民築堤堵水而耕。

translations.literal: Guodong memorialized: "The nine prefectures and counties of Xiangyin, Baling, Huarong, Anxiang, Li, Wuling, Longyang, Yuanjiang, and Yiyang ring around Lake Dongting; the inhabitants build dikes to hold back the water and farm.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong wrote: "Nine prefectures and counties—Xiangyin, Baling, Huarong, Anxiang, Li, Wuling, Longyang, Yuanjiang, and Yiyang—ring Lake Dongting. Their people farm behind dikes that hold back the lake.

sentences.zh: 地勢卑下，江漲反灌入湖，隄岸衝決，現有四百餘處。

translations.literal: The terrain is low; when the Yangtze rises it flows back into the lake, the dikes burst, and at present there are more than four hundred breaches.
translations.idiomatic: The land lies low; when the Yangtze swells it pours back into the lake, the dikes give way, and more than four hundred breaches are open now.

sentences.zh: 正飭刻期完築，務加高培厚，工程堅固。

translations.literal: We are now pressing to finish them on schedule, striving to raise, thicken, and make the works solid.
translations.idiomatic: We are pressing to finish on schedule—raising the banks, thickening them, and making the work hold.

sentences.zh: 」僉都御史申大成奏貴州屯田，民間賤價頂種，易啟紛爭。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Shen Dacheng memorialized on Guizhou garrison fields: the people were planting at low prices by sublease, which easily provoked disputes.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Shen Dacheng reported on Guizhou garrison land: peasants were subleasing at cut-rate prices, which bred quarrels.

sentences.zh: 請仿民田買賣，畝納稅五錢，給照為業，並推行各省。

translations.literal: He asked that sales follow the model of private farmland, with five mace tax per mu and a license as proof of tenure, and that this be extended to every province.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed treating sales like private farmland—five mace tax per mu, a license as title—and extending the rule to every province.

sentences.zh: 國棟疏言：「湖南屯田瘠薄，應分別差等，微價頂種，令完稅五錢，給照如時價平買。

translations.literal: Guodong memorialized: "Hunan garrison fields are poor soil; they should be graded by quality, with sublease at a slight price, completion of the five-mace tax, and licenses issued at fair market value.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong replied: "Hunan's garrison fields are thin; grade them by quality, allow cheap sublease, collect the five-mace tax, and issue licenses at fair market price.

sentences.zh: 未過戶者，視屯糧石稅五錢，已過戶者二錢。

translations.literal: For those not yet transferred, regard the garrison grain tax at five mace per shi; for those already transferred, two mace.
translations.idiomatic: Where title has not changed, take five mace per shi of garrison grain; where it has, two mace.

sentences.zh: 龍陽、武陵、長靖諸屯賦重，按券值兩稅三分。

translations.literal: For the heavy-tax garrisons of Longyang, Wuling, and Changjing, levy three mace per tael of deed value.
translations.idiomatic: For the heavily taxed garrisons of Longyang, Wuling, and Changjing, levy three mace per tael of deed value.

sentences.zh: 」均下部議行。

translations.literal: " All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " All were sent to the ministries for approval and execution.

sentences.zh: 曾靜、張熙事起，上令侍郎杭奕祿至湖南會鞫。

translations.literal: When the affair of Zeng Jing and Zhang Xi arose, the Emperor ordered Vice Minister Hang Yilu to come to Hunan and join in the interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zeng Jing and Zhang Xi case broke out, the Emperor sent Vice Minister Hang Yilu to Hunan to join the examination.

sentences.zh: 國棟聽靜自列，未窮究黨羽，允禩、允禟門下太監以罪徙廣西，流言於路，直隸、河南督撫俱疏上聞。

translations.literal: Guodong heard Jing enumerate his own crimes but did not pursue his associates; eunuchs in the households of Yin Si and Yin Tang, banished to Guangxi for crimes, spread rumors on the road, and the governors of Zhili and Henan all memorialized to report.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong let Jing list his own crimes but did not hunt down accomplices. Eunuchs from the households of the princes Yin Si and Yin Tang, banished to Guangxi for crimes, spread rumors along the road; the governors of Zhili and Henan all reported it.

sentences.zh: 國棟奏言：「湖南監送兵役未聞一語。

translations.literal: Guodong memorialized: "In Hunan the escort soldiers and clerks were not heard to utter a single word."
translations.idiomatic: Guodong wrote: "In Hunan the escort guards were not heard to speak a word of it."

sentences.zh: 」又茶陵民陳蒂西傳播流言，敕國棟按鞫，亦不得實證，坐是失上指，奪官，召還京。

translations.literal: Again, a Chaling commoner named Chen Dix spread rumors; the Emperor ordered Guodong to investigate and interrogate, but again no solid proof was obtained; for this he lost the Emperor's favor, was stripped of office, and recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: A Chaling commoner, Chen Dixi, was also spreading talk; the Emperor ordered Guodong to investigate, but again found no proof. He fell from favor, lost his post, and was recalled to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 八年，命治刑部侍郎事，署山東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to handle the duties of Vice Minister of Punishments and to act as Governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was put in charge of vice-ministerial business at Punishments and acted as Shandong governor.

sentences.zh: 九年，河南祥符、封丘等縣水災，命往治賑。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when Xiangfu, Fengqiu, and other counties in Henan suffered flood disaster, he was ordered to go and manage relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year floods hit Xiangfu, Fengqiu, and other Henan counties; he was sent to manage relief.

sentences.zh: 迭署江蘇、浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: He served in succession as acting Governor of Jiangsu and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He acted in turn as governor of Jiangsu and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十年，仍還刑部。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he returned again to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he returned to Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以議福建民藍厚正殺兄獄失當，吏議降調。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, because his deliberation in the case of the Fujian commoner Lan Houzheng, who had killed his elder brother, was improper, the personnel office recommended demotion.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he mishandled deliberation in the case of Lan Houzheng, a Fujian man who had killed his elder brother; the personnel office recommended demotion.

sentences.zh: 十三年，復命署刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was again ordered to act as Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was again made acting vice minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 許容，河南虞城人。

translations.literal: Xu Rong was a native of Yucheng in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Rong came from Yucheng in Henan.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十年舉人，授陝西府谷知縣。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year of Kangxi he passed the provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Fugu in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 50 he passed the provincial exam and became magistrate of Fugu in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 內遷工部員外郎，考選廣西道御史。

translations.literal: Transferred within the capital to an assistant department director in the Ministry of Works, he was selected by examination as a censor of the Guangxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Called to the capital as an assistant director in Works, he was chosen censor for the Guangxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，改會考府郎中，仍兼御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was changed to director of the Metropolitan Examination Office while still retaining his censor's post.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he became director of the Metropolitan Examination Office while keeping his censor's title.

sentences.zh: 出為直隸口北道，遷陝西按察使。

translations.literal: He went out as intendant of Koubei in Zhili and was transferred to Judicial Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Zhili's Koubei intendant, then became Shaanxi judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 劾河東巡鹽御史馬喀以積鹽變價入己，上奪馬喀官，命兼管河東巡鹽御史，按治。

translations.literal: He impeached the Hedong Salt Circuit Censor Ma Ka for taking into his own purse the proceeds of selling accumulated salt; the Emperor stripped Ma Ka of office, ordered Rong to take concurrent charge of the Hedong salt circuit, and conduct the investigation.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Hedong salt-circuit censor Ma Ka for pocketing proceeds from selling stockpiled salt. The Emperor stripped Ma Ka and put Rong in charge of the circuit to investigate.

sentences.zh: 尋聞容刑逼商人，解容任，令總督岳鍾琪覆按。

translations.literal: Before long word came that Rong had tortured merchants under interrogation; the Emperor relieved Rong of his post and ordered Governor Yue Zhongqi to reinvestigate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon reports said Rong had tortured merchants under interrogation. The Emperor removed him and told Governor Yue Zhongqi to reinvestigate.

sentences.zh: 鍾琪言容無刑逼商人事，上擢浙江布政使。

translations.literal: Zhongqi said Rong had not tortured merchants; the Emperor promoted him to Financial Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqi found no torture; the Emperor promoted Rong to Zhejiang financial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，代國棟為浙江觀風整俗使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he replaced Guodong as Zhejiang Commissioner for Observing Customs and Reforming Morals.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he replaced Guodong as Zhejiang commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋偕廣東巡撫楊文乾清察福建倉庫。

translations.literal: Before long he joined Guangdong Governor Yang Wengan in auditing the Fujian granaries and treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Guangdong governor Yang Wengan in auditing Fujian's granaries and treasuries.

sentences.zh: 六年，遭母喪，給假治喪畢，命仍還浙江。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he suffered his mother's mourning; leave was granted to complete the rites, and he was then ordered to return to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year his mother died; after mourning leave he was ordered back to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 旋擢甘肅巡撫，以蔡仕舢代為浙江觀風整俗使。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Governor of Gansu; Cai Shinan replaced him as Zhejiang Commissioner for Observing Customs and Reforming Morals.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Gansu governor; Cai Shinan replaced him in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 容疏議更正律例，出贓過付人宜視完贓減二等，得贓者完贓減一等，倍完方減二等，連斃二命宜加等。

translations.literal: Rong memorialized on correcting the code: handing over stolen goods after the fact should be treated like full restitution with two degrees' reduction; the receiver of stolen goods with full restitution should have one degree's reduction, and only with double restitution two degrees'; taking two lives in succession should add a degree.
translations.idiomatic: Rong proposed code changes: surrendering loot after the fact should count like full restitution with two degrees off the sentence; a receiver who made full restitution one degree off, double restitution two; consecutive homicides should add a degree.

sentences.zh: 上皆謂不當，責容愚妄。

translations.literal: The Emperor said all were improper and rebuked Rong as foolish and reckless.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rejected every point and called Rong foolish and reckless.

sentences.zh: 八年，師徵噶爾丹，上以容治軍需多推諉，命尚書查弼納赴陝西為之董理。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when troops were raised against Galdan, the Emperor said Rong in managing military supplies often shirked responsibility and ordered Minister Zhabina to go to Shaanxi to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, with troops raised against Galdan, the Emperor said Rong kept shirking supply duties and sent Minister Zhabina to Shaanxi to supervise.

sentences.zh: 及事竟，上諭容曰：「此次軍需，朕為挽將覆之轍，回已頹之波，救汝身家性命。

translations.literal: When the affair was concluded, the Emperor instructed Rong: "This time with military supplies, I turned back the overturned cart and recalled the wave already broken—I saved your person and your family's lives.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended, the Emperor told him: "This time on army supplies I pulled back a cart about to overturn and a wave already spent—I saved your life and your family's.

sentences.zh: 較自御史五年內擢至巡撫之恩大矣！

translations.literal: That grace is greater than promoting you from censor to governor within five years!
translations.idiomatic: That is a greater grace than raising you from censor to governor in five years!

sentences.zh: 汝當知之。

translations.literal: You must know this."
translations.idiomatic: Know that well."

sentences.zh: 」上聞容追逋賦抵兵餉，限一年全完，民以大擾。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard that Rong was pressing arrears in tax to meet military funds, limiting completion to one year, and the people were greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: The court heard he was pressing tax arrears into military funds with a one-year deadline, and the people were in uproar.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「朕念甘肅自軍興以來，輓運轉輸，資於民力，特將雍正八年額徵錢糧蠲免。

translations.literal: An edict said: "I reflect that since military operations began in Gansu, transport and relay have rested on the people's strength; I specially remitted the assessed grain tax of the eighth year of Yongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran: "Since war began in Gansu, transport has rested on the people. I specially remitted the assessed grain tax of Yongzheng 8.

sentences.zh: 容何得於蠲免之年行催徵之舉？

translations.literal: How could Rong in a year of remission carry out collection and pressing?
translations.idiomatic: How could Rong press collection in a year of remission?

sentences.zh: 令即停止。

translations.literal: Order it stopped at once."
translations.idiomatic: Stop it at once."

sentences.zh: 」九年，復以容查核錢糧過刻，諭毋累民。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, again because Rong's audit of grain and funds was too harsh, he was instructed not to burden the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year his grain audit was again too harsh; he was told not to burden the people.

sentences.zh: 十二年，疏劾丁憂知府李綺虧空軍需，綺，衛兄也。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he memorialized impeaching Prefect Li Qi, on mourning leave, for a shortfall in military supplies; Qi was the elder brother of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he impeached mourning-leave prefect Li Qi for a shortfall in military supplies; Qi was Wei's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 上知容與衛有怨，戒容毋遷怒報復。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew Rong bore a grudge against Wei and warned Rong not to vent anger in revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Rong bore a grudge against Wei, the Emperor warned him not to settle scores.

sentences.zh: 容旋奏檄綺赴蘭州，虧空七千有奇，限半年回籍措繳。

translations.literal: Rong soon memorialized ordering Qi to proceed to Lanzhou; the shortfall was more than seven thousand, with a limit of half a year to return home and raise funds to pay.
translations.idiomatic: Rong soon ordered Qi to Lanzhou; the shortfall exceeded seven thousand taels, with half a year to return home and raise payment.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「所虧既有田房可抵，但當速遣回籍折變完補，何須勒限逼迫？

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed: "Since there is farmland and houses that can be applied to the debt, he should simply be sent home at once to sell and make full restitution—why impose a deadline and press him?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "He has land and houses to cover the debt. Send him home at once to sell and pay in full—why set a deadline and hound him?

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，固原、環二縣歉收，容請借給貧民三月口糧，大口日三合，小口日二合。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, when Guyuan and Huan counties had poor harvests, Rong requested lending the poor three months' grain rations—three he for adults per day, two for children.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1, when Guyuan and Huan had poor harvests, Rong asked to lend the poor three months' grain—three he a day for adults, two for children.

sentences.zh: 高宗諭曰：「政莫先於愛民。

translations.literal: Gaozong instructed: "In government nothing comes before cherishing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong wrote: "In government nothing comes before loving the people.

sentences.zh: 甘肅用兵以來，百姓急公踴躍。

translations.literal: Since troops were used in Gansu, the common people have rushed to serve the public with zeal.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Gansu campaigns the people have served the state with zeal.

sentences.zh: 今值歉收，當加恩賑恤。

translations.literal: Now that harvests have failed, grace in relief and succor should be increased.
translations.idiomatic: Now that harvests have failed, add grace in relief.

sentences.zh: 汝治事實心，而理財過刻。

translations.literal: You handle affairs with a sincere heart, yet in managing finances you are too harsh.
translations.idiomatic: You are sincere in office, but too harsh in money matters.

sentences.zh: 國家救濟貧民，非較量錙銖時也。

translations.literal: When the state relieves the poor, this is not the time to haggle over cash and ounces.
translations.idiomatic: When the state feeds the poor, this is not the hour to count cash and ounces.

sentences.zh: 」尋，專筦軍儲大臣劉於義奏請加賑兩月，上責容褊隘卑庸，命解任。

translations.literal: " Before long the minister in sole charge of military stores, Liu Yuyi, memorialized requesting two more months of added relief; the Emperor rebuked Rong as narrow-minded, base, and mediocre and ordered him relieved of office.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Liu Yuyi, minister in charge of army stores, asked for two more months of relief. The Emperor called Rong narrow, base, and mediocre and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 於義及陝西總督查郎阿劾容匿災殃民，奪官逮詣京師論罪，赦免。

translations.literal: Yuyi and Shaanxi Governor Zhalang'a impeached Rong for concealing disaster and harming the people; his office was stripped and he was arrested and brought to the capital for judgment, then pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyi and Shaanxi governor Zhalang'a accused him of concealing famine and harming the people; he was stripped, arrested, and brought to Beijing for trial, then pardoned.

sentences.zh: 二年，署山西布政使。

translations.literal: In the second year he acted as Financial Commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he acted as Shanxi financial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年，調江蘇，署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Jiangsu and acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he moved to Jiangsu as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 四年，遭父喪，去官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he suffered his father's mourning and left office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year his father died and he left office.

sentences.zh: 五年，命署湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was ordered to act as Governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was ordered to act as Hunan governor.

sentences.zh: 請終喪，不許。

translations.literal: He requested to complete mourning; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to finish mourning; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 服闋，真除。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he received regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he received a regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 八年，以劾糧道謝濟世狂縱營私失實，奪官，發順義城工效力。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, for impeaching Grain Intendant Xie Jishi as reckless and profiteering on a charge that did not stand, he was stripped of office and sent to labor on the Shunyi city works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he impeached grain intendant Xie Jishi for recklessness and profiteering on charges that failed; he lost his post and was sent to labor on the Shunyi city works.

sentences.zh: 事互詳濟世傳。

translations.literal: The matter is given in full in Jishi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is told at length in Jishi's biography.

sentences.zh: 九年，復命署湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was again ordered to act as Governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was again made acting Hubei governor.

sentences.zh: 御史陳大玠等疏諍，謂容既以欺罔得罪，不當復用，上命罷之。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Dayu and others memorialized in remonstrance, saying that since Rong had been convicted of deception he ought not be employed again; the Emperor ordered him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Dayu and others protested that a man convicted of deception should not be reused; the Emperor dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 十五年，上巡中岳，迎謁，復原銜。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, when the Emperor toured the Central Peak, Rong came out to welcome him and his former rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, on the tour of the Central Peak, Rong came to welcome the throne and his former rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 尋授內閣學士。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed a Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 以病乞歸，卒。

translations.literal: He begged to return home on grounds of illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave for illness, went home, and died.

sentences.zh: 蔡仕舢，福建南安人。

translations.literal: Cai Shinan was a native of Nan'an in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Shinan came from Nan'an in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十二年舉人。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial exam in Kangxi 32.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，自刑部主事考選御史，出為浙江糧道。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, from principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments he was selected by examination as a censor and went out as Grain Intendant of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 58 he rose from a Punishments secretary to censor by examination and went out as Zhejiang grain intendant.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，授僉都御史，充浙江觀風整俗使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and made Zhejiang Commissioner for Observing Customs and Reforming Morals.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 6 he became vice censor-in-chief and Zhejiang commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七年，署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he acted as governor.

sentences.zh: 八年，坐事降調。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, for an offense he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year an offense brought demotion.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「浙江風俗已漸改移，又有總督李衛善於訓導，不必再遣觀風整俗使。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed: "The customs of Zhejiang have already gradually changed; moreover Governor Li Wei is skilled at instruction and guidance—there is no need to send another Commissioner for Observing Customs and Reforming Morals."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Zhejiang customs have already shifted, and Governor Li Wei is skilled at guidance—there is no need for another commissioner."

sentences.zh: 」仕舢旋卒。

translations.literal: Shinan soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Shinan died soon after.

sentences.zh: 論曰：海望、莽鵠立皆逮事聖祖，雍正、乾隆間參與政事。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Hai Wang and Mang Hulu both served the Sage Ancestor and in the Yongzheng and Qianlong periods took part in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The historians remark: Hai Wang and Mang Hulu both served Kangxi and took part in government under Yongzheng and Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 海望聞世宗末命，在軍機處較久，雖建樹未宏，要為當時親信大臣。

translations.literal: Hai Wang heard Shizong's final command; he served long in the Grand Council—though his achievements were not broad, he was nonetheless a trusted great minister of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Hai Wang heard Yongzheng's deathbed command and served long on the Grand Council. His achievements were not vast, but he was among the emperor's trusted ministers.

sentences.zh: 杭奕祿使安南，傅鼐諭噶爾丹策零，皆不辱君命，傅鼐尤知兵。

translations.literal: Hang Yilu went as envoy to Annan; Fu Nai instructed Galdan Tseren—both did not disgrace the imperial commission; Fu Nai especially understood warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Hang Yilu went to Annan; Fu Nai addressed Galdan Tseren—neither disgraced his commission, and Fu Nai above all knew war.

sentences.zh: 儀領屯田，有惠於鄉州。

translations.literal: Chen Yi oversaw garrison fields and brought benefit to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi directed garrison agriculture and brought benefit to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 師恕、國棟等使車問俗，與民為安靜。

translations.literal: Shishu, Guodong, and the others sent out chariots to inquire into local customs and kept the people in quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Shishu, Guodong, and the rest toured to study local custom and kept the people at peace.

sentences.zh: 以皆世宗特置之官，特謹而書之。

translations.literal: Because all were offices specially established by Shizong, they are recorded here with particular care.
translations.idiomatic: Because these were all offices Yongzheng created for special purposes, they are set down here with particular care.

sentences.zh: 杭奕祿又與史貽直宣諭陝西，非專官，貽直相高宗，故不著於斯篇。

translations.literal: Hang Yilu also went with Shi Yizhi to proclaim an imperial message in Shaanxi—not a dedicated post; Yizhi became a minister under Gaozong, and so is not recorded in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Hang Yilu also went with Shi Yizhi to proclaim the throne's will in Shaanxi—but that was not a dedicated post. Yizhi rose under Qianlong to ministerial rank and is therefore not included in this chapter.
